  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Goodwill&#160;</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Goodwill is tested for impairment annually, on October 31<sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;">st</sup>, with additional reviews performed quarterly or more frequently if events or circumstances indicate there may be impairment.&#160; We have one reporting unit, Community Banking.&#160; If we elect to perform a qualitative assessment, we evaluate factors such as macroeconomic conditions, industry and market considerations, overall financial performance, changes in stock price, and progress towards stated objectives in determining if it is more likely than not that the fair value of our reporting unit is less than its carrying amount. If we conclude that it is more likely than not that the fair value of our reporting unit is less than its carrying amount, a quantitative test is performed; otherwise, no further testing is required. The quantitative test consists of comparing the fair value of our reporting unit to its carrying amount, including goodwill.&#160;If the fair value of our reporting unit is greater than its book value, no goodwill impairment exists.&#160;If the carrying amount of our reporting unit is greater than its calculated fair value, a goodwill impairment charge is recognized for the difference.&#160;We performed a quantitative assessment for the annual test on October 31, 2025, which resulted in no goodwill impairment. For additional information, see Note&#160;8, &#8220;G<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">oodwill </span>and Other Intangible Assets,&#8221; to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Item 8 of this report.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;"><b>Non-GAAP Financial Measures</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">In addition to financial statements prepared in accordance with GAAP, we use certain non-GAAP financial measures that provide useful information for financial and operational decision making, evaluating trends, and comparing financial results to other financial institutions. The non-GAAP financial measures presented in this report include certain financial measures presented on a fully taxable equivalent (&#8220;FTE&#8221;) basis. While we believe certain non-GAAP financial measures enhance the understanding of our business and performance, they are supplemental and not a substitute for, or more important than, financial measures prepared in accordance with GAAP and may not be comparable to those reported by other financial institutions. The reconciliations of non-GAAP to GAAP measures are presented below.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We believe FTE basis is the preferred industry measurement of net interest income and provides better comparability between taxable and tax exempt amounts. We use this non-GAAP financial measure to monitor net interest income performance and to manage the composition of our balance sheet. FTE basis adjusts for the tax benefits of income from certain tax exempt loans and investments using the federal statutory income tax rate of 21%.   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>2025 Compared to 2024</i>.&#160; Pre-tax&#160;income declined $2.57 million, or 3.91%, compared to 2024.&#160; The decline was primarily driven by a $7.74 million increase in noninterest expense and a $1.86 million reduction in net interest income.&#160; These pressures were partially offset by a $3.52 million decrease in the provision for credit losses and a $3.50 million increase in noninterest income.&#160; The increase of noninterest expense was largely attributable to higher salaries and employee benefits of $4.73 million, along with a $2.91 million in merger-related costs associated with the Hometown acquisition.&#160; The lower provision for credit losses reflected a smaller loan portfolio and continued favorable credit performance.&#160; Growth in noninterest income was primarily due to a $3.39 million increase in service charges on deposits and other service fees.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>2024&#160;Compared to 2023</i>.&#160; Pre-tax&#160;income increased $3.72&#160;million, or 6.00% compared to 2023.&#160; The increase was primarily attributable to a&#160;decrease in provision for credit losses of $4.39 million, or 54.95% offset by a decrease in net interest income of $1.22 million, or 0.95%.&#160; Provision for credit losses totaled $3.60 million for 2024 compared to $7.99 million in 2023.&#160; The provision for credit losses in 2023 included $1.61 million recorded for the day two provision for the acquisition of the Surrey loan portfolio. Net interest income totaled $126.47 million for 2024 compared to $127.68 million in 2023.&#160; The decrease in net interest income is primarily attributable to an increase in deposit interest expense due to&#160;increased rates on interest-bearing deposits.&#160; Non interest income&#160;increased $1.94 million, or 5.17% offset by an increase in non interest expense of $1.39 million, or 1.46%.</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>2025 Compared to 2024</i>. Net interest income represented 74.40% of total net interest and noninterest income in 2025, compared to 76.25% in 2024.&#160; The 1.85 percentage-point decline reflects a $1.85 million, or 1.47%, decrease in net interest income and a $3.50 million, or 8.88%, increase in noninterest income.&#160; On an FTE&#160;basis, net interest income decreased $1.86 million, or 1.46%.&#160; Net interest margin and net interest spread experienced modest changes year over year.&#160; Net interest margin declined 2 basis points to 4.42%, while net interest spread increased 1 basis point to 4.04%.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Average earning assets decreased $27.32 million, or 0.96%, due to decreases in both the average balance of loans of $127.67&#160;million, or 5.15%, and the average balance of securities available-for-sale&#160;of $31.80&#160;million, or 18.59%.&#160; These decreases were&#160;offset by&#160;an increase in interest-bearing deposits with banks of $132.15&#160;million, or 63.96%.&#160; The yield on earning assets decreased&#160;8&#160;basis points, or 1.56%, due to an asset balance shift from higher-yielding loans to lower-yielding interest-bearing deposit accounts held with banks. In addition, non-cash accretion decreased $813 thousand in 2025 to $2.08&#160;million, compared to a&#160;2024 balance of $2.90&#160;million.&#160; The impact of non-cash purchase accounting accretion income&#160;on&#160;the FTE net interest margin was 8&#160;basis points for&#160;2025&#160;compared to 10&#160;basis points in 2024.&#160; The average loan to deposit ratio declined to 88.81% in 2025, compared to 92.93% in 2024.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Average interest-bearing liabilities, which consist of interest-bearing deposits and borrowings, decreased $10.16 million, or 0.57%, primarily due to a decrease in interest-bearing deposits of $9.69&#160;million, or 0.54%.&#160; Interest-bearing demand deposits decreased $1.77&#160;million, or 0.27%, and time deposits decreased $25.49&#160;million, or 10.36%.&#160; These decreases were offset by an increase in savings&#160;deposits of $17.58&#160;million or 2.00%.&#160; The yield on interest-bearings liabilities decreased&#160;9&#160;basis points, or 8.18%,&#160;primarily due to an average balance shift from higher rate time deposits to lower rate savings deposits.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>2024&#160;Compared to 2023</i>.&#160; &#160;</p>
  <div style="font-size:10pt">
   <div style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif">
    Net interest income comprised&#160;76.25% of total net interest and noninterest income in 2024&#160;compared to 77.32% in 2023.&#160;&#160;Net interest income decreased $
    <span style="background-color:#ffffff">1.22</span>&#160;million, or 0.95
    <span style="background-color:#ffffff">%</span>.&#160; &#160;On a FTE basis net interest income decreased $1.22 million, or 0.95%. There was no change in the&#160;FTE net interest margin; the&#160;FTE net interest spread decreased
    <span style="background-color:#ffffff">&#160;22</span>
    <span style="background-color:#ffffff">&#160;basis po</span>ints.&#160; The decrease was primarily driven by an increase in interest expense due to increases in rates paid on interest-bearing deposits.
   </div>
   <div style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif">
    &#160;
   </div>
  </div>
  <div style="font-size:10pt">
   <div style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif">
    Average earning assets decreased $24.43&#160;million, or 0.85%, due to decreases in both the average balance of securities available for sale of $127.31 million, or 42.67%, and the average balance of loans of $57.15 million, or 2.25%.&#160; These decreases were&#160;offset by&#160;an increase in interest-bearing deposits with banks of $160.03 million, or 343.40%.&#160; The yield on earning assets increased 36 basis points, or 7.55% and is attributable to an increase in interest income of $8.97 million, or 6.52%.&#160; Interest income for interest-bearing deposits with banks increased $8.37 million, or 336.62%.&#160; This increase was primarily driven by an increase in the average balance&#160;as noted above offset by a decrease in the yield of 8 basis points.&#160; Interest income on loans also increased $3.18 million, or 2.50%.&#160; The increase was primarily due to an increase in yield of 25 basis points offset by a decrease in the average balance of $57.15 million.&#160; Interest income on securities available for sale decreased $2.57 million, or 31.65%.&#160; The yield increased 52 basis points, however, the average balance decreased $127.31 million, or 42.67%.&#160; The average loan to&#160;deposit ratio decreased to 92.93% from 93.04% in 2023.&#160; Non-cash accretion increased&#160;$155&#160;thousand, or 5.65% to $2.90&#160;million.&#160; The impact of non-cash purchase accounting accretion income on the FTE net interest margin was 10&#160;basis points for&#160;2024&#160;compared to 9 basis points in 2023.
   </div>
  </div>
  <div style="font-size:10pt">
   <div style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif">
    &#160;
   </div>
   <div style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif">
    Average interest-bearing liabilities, which consist of interest-bearing deposits and borrowings, decreased $17.26&#160;million, or 0.96%, primarily due to a decrease in interest-bearing deposits of $14.69 million, or 0.81%.&#160; Interest-bearing demand deposits decreased $23.95 million, or 3.49%, and time deposits decreased $21.92&#160;million, or 8.18%.&#160; Savings&#160;deposits increased $31.19&#160;million or 3.68%.&#160; The yield on interest-bearings liabilities increased 58&#160;basis points and is primarily due to increased rates paid on interest-bearing deposit liabilities.
   </div>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Provision for Credit&#160;Losses</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>2025 Compared to 2024</i>.&#160; The provision charged to operations decreased $3.52&#160;million compared to 2024.&#160; The provision expense of $72&#160;thousand&#160;was comprised of $58 thousand&#160;related to provision expense for loans and $14 thousand related to provision expense&#160;for unfunded loan commitments.&#160; Provision for credit losses for loans of $58 thousand&#160;was recorded compared to the provision of $4.00&#160;million recorded in 2024.&#160; The&#160;decrease in provision is due a loan portfolio balance decline of $101.33 million from 2024 to 2025, along with continued strong credit&#160;performance.&#160; &#160;As noted, a $14 thousand provision for loan commitments was recorded in 2025 compared to $405 thousand recovery of provision recorded in 2024.&#160;&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>2024&#160;Compared to 2023</i>.&#160;&#160;The provision charged to operations decreased $4.39&#160;million compared to the prior year.&#160; The provision expense of $3.60&#160;million was comprised of $4.00&#160;million related to provision expense for loans and a recovery of provision of $405&#160;thousand for unfunded loan commitments.&#160; Provision for credit losses for loans of $4.00&#160;million was recorded compared to the provision of $8.44&#160;million recorded in 2023.&#160; The&#160;decrease in provision is primarily due a much smaller required credit loss provision as the loan portfolio has experienced a decrease&#160;of $156.21 million.&#160; Additionally, $1.61 million of the provision in the prior year was&#160;attributable to day two provision for the Surrey portfolio.&#160; As noted above, a recovery of provision for loan commitments was recorded in 2024&#160;of&#160; $405 thousand compared to&#160;a recovery of provision of $450 thousand in 2023.&#160;&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><br/> <i>2025 Compared to 2024</i>. Noninterest income comprised 25.60% of total net interest and noninterest income in&#160;2025 compared to 23.75% in&#160;2024, with noninterest income increasing&#160;$3.50&#160;million,&#160;or 8.88%, in 2025.&#160; The 2025 increase is driven mostly by a $3.39 million increase in&#160;service charges on deposits and other service charges and fees. The increase is primarily attributable to increases in non-sufficient funds fees of $2.45 million and interchange income of $854 thousand.</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>2024 Compared to 2023</i>.&#160; &#160;Noninterest income comprised 23.75% of total net interest and noninterest income in&#160;2024&#160;compared to 22.68% in&#160;2023.&#160; Noninterest income increased $1.94 million,&#160;or 5.17%.&#160; Other operating income increased $850 thousand, or 15.04%.&#160; Other operating income for 2024 included a gain of $825 thousand from the sale of two closed branch properties,&#160;while other operating&#160;income for the same period of 2023 included a gain of $204 thousand for the sale of one&#160;closed branch property.&#160;&#160;In addition, other operating income for 2024, included a holdback payment of $184 thousand related to a prior divestiture of an insurance agency.&#160; Other service charges and fees increased $745 thousand, or 5.46%.&#160; The increase is primarily attributable to an increase in net interchange income of $709&#160;thousand.</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>2025 Compared to 2024</i>.&#160; Non interest expense increased $7.74&#160;million, or 8.01%, in 2025 compared to 2024.&#160; The increase is attributed mostly to increases in salaries and employee benefits of&#160;$4.73&#160;million, merger expense of $2.91 million and other operating expense of $1.00&#160;million.&#160; The increase in salaries and employee benefits is&#160;driven by&#160;a $1.27 million increase in salary expense and a $3.24 million increase in incentive compensation.&#160; The increase in merger expense is related to the Hometown acquisition.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>2024 Compared to 2023</i>.&#160;&#160;Non interest expense increased $1.39 million, or 1.46%.&#160; Salaries and employee benefits increased $1.82 million, other operating expense increased $1.06 million, and service fees increased $734 thousand.&#160; The increases in non-interest expense is primarily due to the addition of the Surrey branches as well as inflationary increases.&#160; Non interest expense for 2023 included non-recurring expense of $2.39 million in merger charges related to the Surrey acquisition.&#160; 2024 included a non-recurring charge of $1.80 million to settle a putative class action lawsuit while 2023 included a non-recurring charge of $3.00 million to accrue for the settlement of the same lawsuit.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Income Tax Expense</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company&#8217;s effective tax rate, income tax as a percent of pre-tax income, may vary significantly from the statutory rate due to permanent differences and available tax credits. Permanent differences are income and expense items excluded by law in the calculation of taxable income. The Company&#8217;s most significant permanent differences generally include interest income on municipal securities and increases in the cash surrender value of life insurance policies.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&#160;</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>2025 Compared to 2024</i>. Income tax expense increased $241&#160;thousand, or 1.71%, due primarily to an increase in pre-tax income.&#160; The effective tax rate increased&#160;to 22.70% in 2025 compared to 21.45% in 2024.&#160;&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&#160;</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>2024 Compared to 2023</i>.&#160;Income tax expense increased $136&#160;thousand, or 0.97% and was primarily due to the increase in pre-tax income.&#160; The effective tax rate decreased to&#160;21.45%&#160;in 2024&#160;compared to 22.52% in 2023.&#160;</p>

Available-for-sale debt securities as of December 31, 2025, decreased $37.16&#160;million, or 21.88%, compared to December 31, 2024. The decrease was primarily due to the sale of $136.71&#160;million in maturities, prepayments, and calls&#160;in securities available for sale; offset by purchases of $93.76&#160;million.&#160; The market value of debt securities available for sale as a percentage of amortized cost was 92.95%&#160;as of December 31, 2025, compared to 91.97%&#160;as of December 31, 2024. There were no held-to-maturity debt securities as of December 31, 2025, or 2024.&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Management evaluates securities for impairment where there has been a decline in fair value below the amortized cost basis of a security to determine whether there is a credit loss associated with the decline in fair value on at least a quarterly basis, and more frequently when economic or market concerns warrant such evaluation. Credit losses are calculated individually, rather than collectively, using a discounted cash flow method, whereby Management compares the present value of expected cash flows with the amortized cost basis of the security.&#160; The credit loss component would be recognized through the provision for credit losses and the creation of an allowance for credit losses. Consideration is given to (1)&#160;the financial condition and near-term prospects of the issuer including looking at default and delinquency rates, (2)&#160;the outlook for receiving the contractual cash flows of the investments, (3)&#160;the length of time and the extent to which the fair value has been less than cost, (4)&#160;our intent and ability to retain its investment in the issuer for a period of time sufficient to allow for any anticipated recovery in fair value or for a debt security whether it is more-likely-than-not that we will be required to sell the debt security prior to recovering its fair value, (5)&#160;the anticipated outlook for changes in the general level of interest rates, (6) credit ratings, (7) third party guarantees, and (8) collateral values. In analyzing an issuer&#8217;s financial condition, management considers whether the securities are issued by the federal government or its agencies, whether downgrades by bond rating agencies have occurred, the results of reviews of the issuer&#8217;s financial condition, and the issuer&#8217;s anticipated ability to pay the contractual cash flows of the investments. All of the U.S. Treasury and Agency-Backed Securities have the full faith and credit backing of the United State Government or one of its agencies. Municipal securities and all other securities that do not have a zero expected credit loss are evaluated quarterly to determine whether there is a credit loss associated with a decline in fair value. Based on the application of the new standard, and that all&#160;debt securities available for sale in an unrealized loss position&#160;as of December 31, 2025, continue to perform as scheduled,&#160;we do not believe that a provision for credit losses is necessary in 2025. We recognized no impairment&#160;charges in earnings associated with debt securities in 2025. For additional information, see Note 1, &#8220;Basis of Presentation and Significant Accounting Policies,&#8221; and Note 3, &#8220;Debt Securities,&#8221; to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Item 8, of this report.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&#160;</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Loans</i><i> Held for Investmen</i><i>t</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Loans held for investment, our largest component of interest income, are grouped into commercial, consumer real estate, and consumer and other loan segments. Each segment is divided into various loan classes based on collateral or purpose.&#160;The general characteristics of each loan segment are as follows:</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;">
   <tbody>
    <tr>
     <td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td>
     <td style="width:18pt;vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt;">&#9679;</p> </td>
     <td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt;">Commercial loans &#8211; This segment consists of loans to small and mid-size industrial, commercial, and service companies.&#160;Commercial real estate projects represent a variety of sectors of the commercial real estate market, including single family and apartment lessors, commercial real estate lessors, and hotel/motel operators. Commercial loan underwriting guidelines require that comprehensive reviews and independent evaluations be performed on credits exceeding predefined size limits. Updates to these loan reviews are done periodically or annually depending on the size of the loan relationship.</p> </td>
    </tr>

     <td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt;">Consumer real estate loans &#8211; This segment consists of largely of loans to individuals within our market footprint for home equity loans and lines of credit and for the purpose of financing residential properties. Residential real estate loan underwriting guidelines require that borrowers meet certain credit, income, and collateral standards at origination.</p> </td>

     <td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt;">Consumer and other loans &#8211; This segment consists of loans to individuals within our market footprint that include, but are not limited to, automobile, credit cards, personal lines of credit,&#160;boats, mobile homes, and other consumer goods. For additional information, see Note 4, &#8220;Loans,&#8221; to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Item 8 of this report.</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><i>&#160;</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Risk Elements</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">We seek to mitigate credit risk by following specific underwriting practices and by ongoing monitoring of our loan portfolio. Our underwriting practices include the analysis of borrowers&#8217; prior credit histories, financial statements, tax returns, and cash flow projections; valuation of collateral based on independent appraisers&#8217; reports; and verification of liquid assets. We believe our underwriting criteria are appropriate for the various loan types we offer; however, losses may occur that exceed the reserves established in our allowance for loan losses. The Company has a loan review function independent of credit administration that performs a risk-based review of a sample of loans and loan relationships in the Company's commercial portfolio and conducts analytical review of credit quality on the Company's non-commercial portfolios.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Nonperforming assets consist of nonaccrual loans, accrual loans contractually past due 90 days or more, modified loans past due 90 days or more,&#160;and other real estate owned ("OREO"). Prior to the adoption of ASU 2022-02, unseasoned troubled debt restructurings ("TDRs") were included in nonperforming assets.&#160; Ongoing activity in the classification and categories of nonperforming loans include collections on delinquencies, foreclosures, loan restructurings, and movements into or out of the nonperforming classification due to changing economic conditions, borrower financial capacity, or resolution efforts.&#160; For additional information, see Note 5, &#8220;Credit Quality,&#8221; to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Item 8 of this report.</p>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Nonperforming assets as of December 31, 2025, decreased&#160;$6.39&#160;million, or 31.09%, from December 31, 2024, with the largest decreases&#160;attributable&#160;to nonaccrual loans of $5.93&#160;million, or 29.84%, and OREO of $521&#160;thousand.&#160; &#160; As of December 31, 2025, nonaccrual loans were largely attributed to single family owner occupied $8.26 million, or 59.22%, non-farm, non-residential real estate $1.27 million, or&#160;9.13%, and commercial and industrial&#160;loans $1.32 million, or&#160;9.45%.&#160; Certain loans included in the nonaccrual category have been written down to estimated realizable value or assigned specific reserves in the allowance for credit losses based on management's estimate of loss at ultimate resolution.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Delinquent loans, comprised of loans 30 days or more past due and nonaccrual loans, totaled $27.85&#160;million as of December 31, 2025, a decrease&#160;of $9.70&#160;million, or 25.83%, compared to $37.55&#160;million as of December 31, 2024. Delinquent loans as a percent of total loans decreased in 2025 to 1.20%, compared to 1.49%&#160;in 2024.&#160; The&#160;delinquent loans consist of past due loans, or&#160;0.60%, of total loans, and nonaccrual loans, or&#160;0.60%, of total loans.&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">When restructuring loans for borrowers experiencing financial difficulty, we generally make concessions in interest rates, loan terms, or amortization terms.&#160; As noted above, ASU 2022-02, eliminated and replaced the accounting guidance for borrowers experiencing financial difficulties previously applied under ASC 310-40, Receivables - Troubled Debt Restructurings by Creditors.&#160; ASU 2022-02, Financial Instruments-Credit Losses (Topic 326), Troubled Debt Restructurings and Vintage Disclosures, discloses loans for borrowers experiencing financial difficulty as modified loans.&#160; Total loans modified as of December 31, 2025, were&#160;$2.44&#160;million as compared to $2.26&#160;million reported as of December 31, 2024.&#160;&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Allowance for Credit</i><i>&#160;</i><i>Losses (ACL)</i></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The ACL reflects management&#8217;s estimate of losses that will result from the inability of our borrowers to make required loan payments. Management uses a systematic methodology to determine its ACL for loans held for investment and certain off-balance-sheet credit exposures. The ACL is a valuation account that is deducted from the amortized cost basis to present the net amount expected to be collected on the loan portfolio. Management considers the effects of past events, current conditions, and reasonable and supportable forecasts on the collectability of the loan portfolio. The Company&#8217;s estimate of its ACL involves a high degree of judgment; therefore, management&#8217;s process for determining expected credit losses may result in a range of expected credit losses. It is possible that others, given the same information, may at any point in time reach a different reasonable conclusion. The Company&#8217;s ACL recorded in the balance sheet reflects management&#8217;s best estimate of expected credit losses. The Company recognizes in net income the amount needed to adjust the ACL for management&#8217;s current estimate of expected credit losses. The Company&#8217;s measurement of credit losses policy adheres to GAAP as well as interagency guidance. The Company's ACL is calculated using collectively evaluated and individually evaluated loans.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">For collectively evaluated loans, the Company in general uses two modeling approaches to estimate expected credit losses. The Company projects the contractual run-off of its portfolio at the segment level and incorporates a prepayment assumption in order to estimate exposure at default. Financial assets that have been individually evaluated can be returned to a pool for purposes of estimating the expected credit loss insofar as their credit profile improves and that the repayment terms were not considered to be unique to the asset.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>

   <div class="PGFTR" style="text-align: center; width: 100%">
    <div class="hf-row">
     <div class="hf-cell PGNUM" style="text-align: center; font-size: 10pt; font-family: Times New Roman;">
      32

     </div>

  </div>
  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">In addition to its own loss experience, management also includes peer bank historical loss experience in its assessment of expected credit losses to determine the ACL. The Company utilized call report data to measure historical credit loss experience with similar risk characteristics within the segments. For the majority of segment models for collectively evaluated loans, the Company incorporated at least one macroeconomic driver either using a statistical regression modeling methodology or simple loss rate modeling methodology.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Included in its systematic methodology to determine its ACL for loans held for investment and certain off-balance-sheet credit exposures,&#160;management considers the need to qualitatively adjust expected credit losses for information not already captured in the loss estimation process. These qualitative adjustments either increase or decrease the quantitative model estimation (i.e. formulaic model results). Each period, the Company considers qualitative factors that are relevant within the qualitative framework.&#160; For further discussion of our Allowance for Credit Losses - See Note 1 - "Basis of Presentation - Significant Accounting Policies".</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">As of&#160;December 31, 2025, the balance of the ACL for loans was $30.76&#160;million, or 1.33%&#160;of total loans. The ACL at December 31, 2025, decreased $4.06&#160;million from the balance of $34.83&#160;million recorded December 31, 2024. This decrease included a provision of $58 thousand&#160;and net&#160;charge-offs for the twelve&#160;months&#160;of $4.12&#160;million. &#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">At December 31, 2025,&#160;the Company also had an allowance for unfunded commitments of $355&#160;thousand&#160;compared to $341&#160;thousand in 2024. The allowance for unfunded commitments is&#160;recorded in Other Liabilities on the balance sheet.&#160;&#160;During 2025,&#160;there was a provision for&#160;credit losses on unfunded commitments of&#160;$14&#160;thousand.&#160; The provision for credit losses on unfunded commitments is&#160;recorded in provision expense&#160;on the Statement of Income.&#160;&#160;</p>
  <p style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;">Management considered the allowance adequate as of December 31, 2025; however, no assurance can be made that additions to the allowance will not be required in future periods. For additional information, see &#8220;Allowance for Credit&#160;Losses or ("ACL")&#8221; in the &#8220;Critical Accounting Policies&#8221; section above and Note 6, &#8220;Allowance for Credit&#160;Losses,&#8221; to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Item 8 of this report.</p>

  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Liquidity</b><b> and Capital Resources</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Liquidity</i></b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Liquidity is a measure of our ability to meet current and future cash flow needs as they become due. The liquidity of a financial institution reflects its ability to meet loan requests, to accommodate possible outflows in deposits and to take advantage of interest rate market opportunities. The ability of a financial institution to meet its current financial obligations is a function of its balance sheet structure that draws together all sources and uses of liquidity. The objective of our liquidity management is to manage cash flow and liquidity reserves so that they are adequate to fund our operations and to meet obligations and other commitments on a timely basis and at a reasonable cost. We seek to achieve this objective and ensure that funding needs are met by maintaining an appropriate level of liquid funds through&#160;asset/liability management, which includes managing the mix and time to maturity of financial assets and financial liabilities on our balance sheet.</p>
  <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Poor or inadequate liquidity risk management may result in a funding deficit that could have a material impact on our operations. We maintain a liquidity risk management policy and contingency funding policy (&#8220;Liquidity Plan&#8221;) to detect potential liquidity issues and protect our depositors, creditors, and shareholders. The Liquidity Plan includes various internal and external indicators that are reviewed on a recurring basis by our Asset/Liability Management Committee (&#8220;ALCO&#8221;) of the Board of Directors. ALCO reviews liquidity risk exposure and policies related to liquidity management; ensures that systems and internal controls are consistent with liquidity policies; and provides accurate reports about liquidity needs, sources, and compliance. The Liquidity Plan involves ongoing monitoring and estimation of potentially credit sensitive liabilities and the sources and amounts of balance sheet and external liquidity available to replace outflows during a funding crisis. The liquidity model incorporates various funding crisis scenarios and a specific action plan is formulated, and activated, when a financial shock that affects our normal funding activities is identified. Generally, the plan will reflect a strategy of replacing liability outflows with alternative liabilities, rather than balance sheet asset liquidity, to the extent that significant premiums can be avoided. If alternative liabilities are not available, outflows will be met through liquidation of balance sheet assets, including unpledged securities. As of December 31, 2025, management is not aware of any events that are reasonably likely to have a material adverse effect on our liquidity, capital resources or operations. In addition, management is not aware of any regulatory recommendations regarding liquidity that would have a material adverse effect on the Company.</p>
  <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">In the ordinary course of business we have entered into contractual obligations and have made other commitments to make future payments. Refer to the accompanying notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Item 8 of this report for the expected timing of such payments as of December 31, 2025. These include payments related to (i) operating leases (Note - 7 Premises, Equipment, and Leases ), (ii) time deposits with stated maturity dates (Note 9 - Deposits), and (iii) commitments to extend credit and standby letters of credit (Note - 19 Litigation, Commitments, and Contingencies).</p>
  <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">As a financial holding company, the Company&#8217;s primary source of liquidity is dividends received from the Bank, which are subject to certain regulatory limitations. Other sources of liquidity include cash, investment securities, and borrowings. As of December 31, 2025, the Company&#8217;s cash reserves and short-term investment securities totaled $36.95&#160;million and&#160;$10.93&#160;million, respectively. &#160;The Company&#8217;s cash reserves and investments provide adequate working capital to meet obligations and projected dividends to shareholders for the next twelve months.</p>
  <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">In addition to cash on hand and deposits with other financial institutions, we rely on customer deposits, cash flows from loans and investment securities, and lines of credit from the FHLB and the FRB&#160;Discount Window to meet potential liquidity demands. These sources of liquidity are immediately available to satisfy deposit withdrawals, customer credit needs, and our operations. Secondary sources of liquidity include approved lines of credit with correspondent banks and unpledged available-for-sale securities. As of December 31, 2025, our unencumbered cash totaled $512.24&#160;million, unused borrowing capacity from the FHLB totaled $301.81&#160;million,&#160;available credit from the FRB Discount Window totaled $5.85&#160;million, available lines from correspondent banks totaled $100.00&#160;million, and unpledged available-for-sale securities totaled $102.83&#160;million.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&#160;</i></p>

  <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Market Risk and Interest Rate </b><b>Sensitivity</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Market risk represents the risk of loss due to adverse changes in current and future cash flows, fair values, earnings, or capital due to movements in interest rates and other factors. Our profitability is largely dependent upon net interest income, which is subject to variation due to changes in the interest rate environment and unbalanced repricing opportunities. We are subject to interest rate risk when interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities reprice at differing times, when underlying rates change at different levels or in varying degrees, when there is an unequal change in the spread between two or more rates for different maturities, and when embedded options, if any, are exercised. ALCO reviews our mix of assets and liabilities with the goal of limiting exposure to interest rate risk, ensuring adequate liquidity, and coordinating sources and uses of funds while maintaining an acceptable level of net interest income given the current interest rate environment. ALCO is also responsible for overseeing the formulation and implementation of policies and strategies to improve balance sheet positioning and mitigate the effect of interest rate changes.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">In order to manage our exposure to interest rate risk, we periodically review internal and third-party simulation models that project net interest income at risk, which measures the impact of different interest rate scenarios on net interest income, and the economic value of equity at risk, which measures potential long-term risk in the balance sheet by valuing our assets and liabilities at fair value under different interest rate scenarios. Simulation results show the existence and severity of interest rate risk in each scenario based on our current balance sheet position, assumptions about changes in the volume and mix of interest-earning assets and interest-bearing liabilities, and estimated yields earned on assets and rates paid on liabilities. The simulation model provides the best tool available to us and the industry for managing interest rate risk; however, the model cannot precisely predict the impact of fluctuations in interest rates on net interest income due to the use of significant estimates and assumptions. Actual results will differ from simulated results due to the timing, magnitude, and frequency of interest rate changes; changes in market conditions and customer behavior; and changes in our strategies that management might undertake in response to a sudden and sustained rate shock.</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
  <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">As of&#160;December 31, 2025, the Federal Open Market Committee set&#160;the benchmark federal funds rate at&#160;a range of 3.50% - 3.75%&#160;basis points. The following table presents the sensitivity of net interest income from immediate and sustained rate shocks in various interest rate scenarios over a twelve-month period for the periods indicated.&#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:BasisOfPresentationAndSignificantAccountingPoliciesTextBlock" id="c3125667" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b><a id="notes" title="notes" href="#"></a>FIRST COMMUNITY BANKSHARES, INC.</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">1.</em></b><b> </b><b>Basis of Presentation and </b><b>Significant </b><b>Accounting Policies</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:BasisOfAccountingPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c141562228" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Basis of Presentation</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">First Community Bankshares, Inc. (the &#8220;Company&#8221;) is a financial holding company incorporated under the laws of the Commonwealth of Virginia. The Company&#8217;s principal executive office is located in&#160;Bluefield, Virginia. The Company provides banking products and services to individual and commercial customers through its wholly owned subsidiary First Community Bank (the &#8220;Bank&#8221;), a Virginia-chartered banking institution founded in <em style="font: inherit;">1874.</em> The Bank offers wealth management and investment advice through its Trust Division and wholly owned subsidiary First Community Wealth Management (&#8220;FCWM&#8221;). Unless the context suggests otherwise, the terms &#8220;First Community,&#8221; &#8220;Company,&#8221; &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;our,&#8221; and &#8220;us&#8221; refer to First Community Bankshares, Inc. and its subsidiaries as a consolidated entity.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:ConsolidationPolicyTextBlock" id="c141562229" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Principles of Consolidation</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company&#8217;s accounting and reporting policies conform with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;) and prevailing practices in the banking industry. The consolidated financial statements include all accounts of the Company and its wholly owned subsidiaries and eliminate all intercompany balances and transactions. The Company operates in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141557908">one</span> business segment, Community Banking, which consists of all operations, including commercial and consumer banking, lending activities, and wealth management.&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company maintains investments in variable interest entities (&#8220;VIEs&#8221;). VIEs are legal entities in which equity investors do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have sufficient equity at risk for the entity to independently finance its activities, or as a group, the holders of the equity investment at risk lack the power through voting or similar rights to direct the activities of the entity that most significantly impact its economic performance, or do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have the obligation to absorb the expected losses of the entity or the right to receive expected residual returns of the entity. Consolidation of a VIE is required if a reporting entity is the primary beneficiary of the VIE. The Company periodically reviews its VIEs and has determined that it is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> the primary beneficiary of any VIE; therefore, the assets and liabilities of these entities are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> consolidated into the financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>&#160;</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:PriorPeriodReclassificationAdjustmentDescription" id="c141562230" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Reclassification</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Certain amounts reported in prior years have been reclassified to conform to the current year&#8217;s presentation. These reclassifications had <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> effect on the Company&#8217;s results of operations, financial position, or net cash flow.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:UseOfEstimates" id="c141562231" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Use of Estimates</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">To prepare financial statements in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America management makes estimates and assumptions based on available information. These estimates and assumptions affect the amounts reported in the financial statements and the disclosures provided, and actual results could differ.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>Summary of Significant Accounting Policies</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b><i>&#160;</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueMeasurementPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c141562232" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Fair Value Measurements</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Fair value is defined as the price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability, in the principal or most advantageous market for the asset or liability, in an orderly transaction between market participants. Market participants are buyers and sellers in the principal market that are independent, knowledgeable, able to transact, and willing to transact.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 18pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; vertical-align: top; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> &#8211; Inputs other than quoted prices included in Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> that are directly or indirectly observable for the asset or liability</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width: 100%; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><tbody><tr style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><td style="width: 18pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</td><td style="width: 18pt; vertical-align: top; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align: top; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> &#8211; Unobservable inputs with little or <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> market activity that require the Company to use reasonable inputs and assumptions</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="background-color: rgb(255, 255, 255); font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company uses fair value measurements to record adjustments to certain financial assets and liabilities on a recurring basis. The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be required to record certain assets at fair value on a nonrecurring basis in specific circumstances, such as evidence of impairment. Methodologies used to determine fair value might be highly subjective and judgmental in nature; therefore, valuations <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em><em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be precise. If the Company determines that a valuation technique change is necessary, the change is assumed to have occurred at the end of the respective reporting period.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>&#160;</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:CashAndCashEquivalentsPolicyTextBlock" id="c141562234" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Cash and Cash Equivalent</i><i>s</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Cash and cash equivalents include cash and due from banks, federal funds sold, and interest-bearing balances on deposit with the Federal Home Loan Bank ("FHLB"), the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond ("FRB"), and correspondent banks that are available for immediate withdrawal.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:MarketableSecuritiesPolicy" id="c141562235" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Investment</i><i> </i><i>Securities</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Management classifies debt securities as held-to-maturity or available-for-sale based on the intent and ability to hold the securities to maturity. Debt securities that the Company has the intent and ability to hold to maturity are classified as held-to-maturity securities and carried at amortized cost. Debt securities <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> classified as held to maturity are classified as available-for-sale securities and carried at estimated fair value. Available-for-sale securities consist of securities the Company intends to hold for indefinite periods of time including securities to be used as part of the Company&#8217;s asset/liability management strategy and securities that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be sold for a variety of reasons. Unrealized gains and losses on available-for-sale securities are included in accumulated other comprehensive income (&#8220;AOCI&#8221;), net of income taxes, in stockholders&#8217; equity. Gains or losses on calls, maturities, or sales of investment securities are recorded based on the specific identification method and included in noninterest income. Premiums are amortized to <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> call date and discounts are&#160;accreted over the life of a security into interest income.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Management evaluates securities for impairment where there has been a decline in fair value below the amortized cost basis of a security to determine whether there is a credit loss associated with the decline in fair value on at least a quarterly basis, and more frequently when economic or market concerns warrant such evaluation. Credit losses are calculated individually, rather than collectively, using a discounted cash flow method, whereby Management compares the present value of expected cash flows with the amortized cost basis of the security.&#160; The credit loss component would be recognized through the provision for credit losses and the creation of an allowance for credit losses. Consideration is given to (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>)&#160;the financial condition and near-term prospects of the issuer including looking at default and delinquency rates, (<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>)&#160;the outlook for receiving the contractual cash flows of the investments, (<em style="font: inherit;">3</em>)&#160;the length of time and the extent to which the fair value has been less than cost, (<em style="font: inherit;">4</em>)&#160;our intent and ability to retain its investment in the issuer for a period of time sufficient to allow for any anticipated recovery in fair value or for a debt security whether it is more-likely-than-<em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that we will be required to sell the debt security prior to recovering its fair value, (<em style="font: inherit;">5</em>)&#160;the anticipated outlook for changes in the general level of interest rates, (<em style="font: inherit;">6</em>) credit ratings, (<em style="font: inherit;">7</em>) <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party guarantees, and (<em style="font: inherit;">8</em>) collateral values. The Company evaluates impairment where there has been a decline in fair value below the amortized cost basis of a security to determine whether there is a credit loss associated with the decline in fair value.&#160; The nature of the collateral is considered along with potential future changes in collateral values, default rates, delinquency rates, <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party guarantees, credit ratings, interest rate changes since purchase, volatility of the security&#8217;s fair&#160;value and historical loss information for financial assets secured with similar collateral among other factors.&#160; Credit losses are calculated individually, rather than collectively, using a discounted cash flow method, whereby management compares the present value of expected cash flows with the amortized cost basis of the security.&#160; The credit loss component would be recognized through the provision for credit losses in the Statement of Income and establish an allowance for credit losses on the Balance Sheet.</p>

   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i><i></i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="fcbc:OtherInvestmentsPolicyTextBlock" id="c141562236" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i><i>Other Investments</i></i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
