   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b></b></p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>FIRST COMMUNITY BANKSHARES, INC.</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</b></p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationsPolicy" id="c141562237" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Business Combinations</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company accounts for business combinations using the acquisition method of accounting as outlined in using Topic <em style="font: inherit;">805</em> of the Financial Accounting Standards Board&#8217;s (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) Accounting Standards Codification (&#8220;ASC&#8221;). Under this method, all identifiable assets acquired, including purchased loans, and liabilities assumed are recorded at fair value. Any excess of the purchase price over the fair value of net assets acquired is recorded as goodwill. In instances where the price of the acquired business is less than the net assets acquired, a gain on the purchase is recorded. Fair values are assigned based on quoted prices for similar assets, if readily available, or appraisals by qualified independent parties for relevant asset and liability categories. Certain financial assets and liabilities are valued using discount models that apply current discount rates to streams of cash flow. Valuation methods require assumptions, which can result in alternate valuations, varying levels of goodwill or bargain purchase gains, or amortization expense or accretion income. Management must make estimates for the useful or economic lives of certain acquired assets and liabilities that are used to establish the amortization or accretion of some intangible assets and liabilities, such as core deposits. Fair values are subject to refinement for up to <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year after the closing date of the acquisition as additional information about the closing date fair values becomes available. Acquisition and divestiture activities are included in the Company&#8217;s consolidated results of operations from the closing date of the transaction. Acquisition and divestiture related costs are recognized in noninterest expense as incurred. For additional information, see &#8220;Purchased Credit Deteriorated&#160;Loans&#8221; and &#8220;Intangible Assets&#8221; below.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:FinanceLoanAndLeaseReceivablesHeldForInvestmentPolicy" id="c141562239" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Loans Held for Investment</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Loans classified as held for investment are originated with the intent to hold indefinitely, until maturity, or until pay-off. Loans held for investment are carried at the principal amount outstanding, net of unearned income and any necessary write-downs to reduce individual loans to net realizable value.&#160;Interest income on performing loans is recognized as interest income at the contractual rate of interest. Loan origination fees, including loan commitment and underwriting fees, are reduced by direct costs associated with loan processing, including salaries, legal review, and appraisal fees. Net deferred loan fees are deferred and amortized over the life of the related loan or commitment period.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Purchased Performing Loans</i><i>.</i> Purchased loans that are deemed to be performing at the acquisition date are accounted for using the contractual cash flow method of accounting, which results in the loans being recorded at fair value with a credit discount. The fair value discount or premium is accreted or amortized, as the case <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be, as an adjustment to yield over the estimated contractual lives of the loans.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>P</i><i>urchased </i><i>C</i><i>redit Deteriorated</i><i>&#160;</i><i>(&#8220;PCD&#8221;) </i><i>Loans</i>.&#160;Purchased credit-deteriorated, otherwise referred to herein as PCD, assets are defined as acquired individual financial assets (or acquired groups of financial assets with similar risk characteristics) that, as of the date of acquisition, have experienced a more-than-insignificant deterioration in credit quality since origination, as determined by the Company&#8217;s assessment. The Company records acquired PCD loans by adding the expected credit losses (i.e. allowance for credit losses) to the purchase price of the financial assets rather than recording through the provision for credit losses in the income statement. The expected credit loss, as of the acquisition date, of a PCD loan is added to the allowance for credit losses. The non-credit discount or premium is the difference between the fair value and the amortized cost basis as of the acquisition date. Subsequent to the acquisition date, the change in the ACL on PCD loans is recognized through the provision for credit losses. The non-credit discount or premium is accreted or amortized, respectively, into interest income over the remaining life of the PCD loan on a level-yield basis. In accordance with the transition requirements within the standard, the Company&#8217;s acquired purchased credit impaired loans were treated as PCD loans.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Individually Evaluated Loans and Nonperforming Assets</i>.&#160; The Company maintains an active and robust problem credit identification system through its ongoing credit review function.&#160; When a loan <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer shares similar risk characteristics with its segment, the asset is assessed to determine whether it should be included in another pool or should be individually evaluated. The Company currently maintains a net book balance threshold of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141557945" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="fcbc:MinimumPrincipalBalanceOfLoansForQuarterlyRatingReview" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">500,000</ix:nonFraction> for individually-evaluated loans. Generally, individually-evaluated loans&#160;are on nonaccrual status. Based on the threshold above, consumer loans will generally remain in pools unless they meet the dollar threshold and foreclosure is probable. The expected credit losses on individually-evaluated loans will be estimated based on discounted cash flow analysis unless the loan meets the criteria for use of the fair value of collateral, either by virtue of an expected foreclosure or through meeting the definition of collateral-dependent. Financial assets that have been individually evaluated can be returned to a pool for purposes of estimating the expected credit loss insofar as their credit profile improves and that the repayment terms were <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered to be unique to the asset.&#160;&#160;The Company follows its nonaccrual policy by reversing contractual interest income in the income statement when the Company places a loan on nonaccrual status. Therefore, Management excludes the accrued interest receivable balance from the amortized cost basis in measuring expected credit losses on the portfolio and does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> record an allowance for credit losses on "AIR".&#160;&#160;The accrual of interest, which is based on the daily amount of principal outstanding, on individually evaluated&#160;loans is generally continued unless the loan becomes delinquent <em style="font: inherit;">90</em> days or more.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Loans are considered past due when either principal or interest payments become contractually delinquent by <em style="font: inherit;">30</em> days or more. The Company&#8217;s policy is to discontinue the accrual of interest, if warranted, on loans based on the payment status, evaluation of the related collateral, and the financial strength of the borrower. Loans that are <em style="font: inherit;">90</em> days or more past due are placed on nonaccrual status. Management <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>elect to continue the accrual of interest when the loan is well secured and in process of collection. When interest accruals are discontinued, interest accrued and <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> collected in the current year is reversed from income, and interest accrued and <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> collected from prior years is charged to the allowance for credit losses. Nonaccrual loans <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be returned to accrual status when all principal and interest amounts contractually due, including past due payments, are brought current; the ability of the borrower to repay the obligation is reasonably assured; and there is generally a period of at least <em style="font: inherit;">six</em> months of repayment performance by the borrower in accordance with the contractual terms.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <ix:exclude>

   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b></b></p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>FIRST COMMUNITY BANKSHARES, INC.</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</b></p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Seriously delinquent loans are evaluated for loss mitigation options. Closed-end retail loans are generally charged off against the allowance for credit&#160;losses when the loans become <em style="font: inherit;">120</em> days past due. Open-end retail loans and residential real estate secured loans are generally charged off when the loans become <em style="font: inherit;">180</em> days past due. Unsecured loans are generally charged off when the loans become <em style="font: inherit;">90</em> days past due. All other loans are charged off against the allowance for credit losses after collection attempts have been exhausted, which generally is within <em style="font: inherit;">120</em> days. Recoveries of loans previously charged off are credited to the allowance for credit losses in the period received.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Effective <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2023, </em>the Company adopted Financial Accounting Standards Board issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">02,</em> Financial Instruments-Credit Losses (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">326</em>), Troubled Debt Restructurings and Vintage Disclosures.&#160; The allowance for credit losses incorporates an estimate of lifetime credit losses and is recorded on each asset upon origination.&#160; The starting point for the estimate of the allowance for credit losses is historical loss information, which includes losses from modifications of receivables to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty.&#160; The Company uses a probability of default/loss given default model to determine the allowance for credit losses.&#160; An assessment of whether a borrower is experiencing financial difficulty is made at the time of the modification.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Because the effect of most modifications made to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty is already included in the allowance for credit losses, a change to the allowance for credit losses is generally <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recorded upon modification.&#160; Occasionally, the Company modifies loans by providing principal forgiveness that is deemed to be uncollectible; therefore, that portion of the loan is written off, resulting in a reduction of the amortized cost basis and a corresponding adjustment to the allowance for credit losses.&#160; Additionally, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>allow a loan to go interest only for a specified period of time.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Other real estate owned (&#8220;OREO&#8221;) acquired through foreclosure, or other settlement, is carried at the lower of cost or fair value less estimated selling costs. The fair value is generally based on current <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party appraisals. When a property is transferred into OREO, any excess of the loan balance over the net realizable fair value is charged against the allowance for credit losses. Operating expenses, gains, and losses on the sale of OREO are included in other noninterest expense in the Company&#8217;s consolidated statements of income after any fair value write-downs are recorded as valuation adjustments.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:CreditLossFinancialInstrumentPolicyTextBlock" id="c141562240" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Allowance for Credit&#160;Losses (ACL)</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company reviews our allowance for credit&#160;losses quarterly to determine if it is sufficient to absorb expected credit losses in the portfolio. This determination requires management to make significant estimates and assumptions. While the Company&#160;uses its best judgment and available information, the ultimate adequacy of the allowance is dependent upon a variety of factors beyond our control, including the performance of our loan portfolio, the economy, changes in interest rates, and the view of regulatory authorities towards loan classifications. These uncertainties <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>result in material changes to the allowance for credit&#160;losses in the near term; however, the amount of the change cannot reasonably be estimated.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The ACL is an estimate of losses that will result from the inability of borrowers to make required loan payments.&#160; The Company established the incremental increase in the ACL at the adoption through&#160;retained earnings and subsequent adjustments will be made through a provision for credit losses charged to earnings.&#160; Loans charged off are recorded against the ACL and subsequent recoveries increase the ACL when they are recognized.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">A systematic methodology is used to determine ACL for loans held for investment and certain off-balance sheet credit exposures.&#160; The ACL is a valuation account that is deducted from the amortized cost basis to present the net amount expected to be collected on the loan portfolio.&#160; The Company&#160;considers the effects of past events, current conditions, and reasonable and supportable forecasts on the collectability of the loan portfolio.&#160; The Company&#8217;s estimate of its ACL involves a high degree of judgement and reflects management&#8217;s best estimate within the range of expected credit losses.&#160; The Company recognizes in net income the amount needed to adjust the ACL for management&#8217;s current estimate of expected credit losses.&#160; The Company&#8217;s ACL is calculated using collectively evaluated and individually evaluated loans.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company collectively evaluates loans that share similar risk characteristics.&#160; In general, loans are segmented by loan purpose.&#160; The Company collectively evaluates loans within the following consumer and commercial segments:&#160; Loans secured by <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">4</em> Family Properties, Home Equity Lines of Credit (&#8220;HELOC&#8221;), Owner Occupied Construction Loans, Consumer Loans, Commercial and Industrial, Multi-family, Non-farm/Non-residential Property, Commercial Construction/A&amp;D/other Land Loans, Agricultural Loans, Loans Secured by Farmland, and Other Consumer Loans (Overdrafts).</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Risk characteristics of residential real estate loans which include loans secured by Single family properties, HELOC, and Owner occupied construction loans are dependent upon individual borrowers who are affected by changes in general economic conditions, real estate valuations, and the demand for housing.&#160; Commercial and Industrial, Multi-family residential, Non-farm/non-residential, Agricultural, and Loans secured by Farmland are similar in that they are generally dependent upon the borrower's internal cash flow from operations to service the debt and changes in general economic conditions.&#160; Commercial construction, Development, and other land loans, Consumer, and&#160;Other consumer loans (open pool) are similar in that they are dependent on changes in general economic conditions.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">For collectively evaluated loans, the Company uses a combination of discounted cash flow and open pool&#160;to estimate expected credit losses.&#160; In addition to its own loss experience, management also includes peer bank historical loss experience in its assessment of expected credit losses to determine the ACL.&#160; The Company utilized call report data to measure its and its peers' historical credit losses experience with similar risk characteristics within the segments over an economic cycle.&#160; The Company&#160;reviewed the historical loss information to appropriately adjust for differences in current asset specific risk characteristics.&#160; Also considered were further adjustments to historical loss information for current conditions and reasonable and supportable forecasts that differ from the conditions that existed for the period over which historical information was evaluated.&#160; For the majority of the segments of collectively evaluated loans, the Company incorporated at least <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> macroeconomic driver&#160;using a statistical regression modeling methodology.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company considers forward-looking information in estimated expected credit losses.&#160; The Company subscribes to a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party service which provides summary detail of dozens of economic forecasts.&#160; Using that information and other publicly available economic forecasts, management determines the economic variables to use for the <em style="font: inherit;">one</em>-year reasonable and supportable forecast period.&#160; Management has determined that the forecast period is consistent with how the Company has historically forecasted for its profitability planning and capital management.&#160; Management has evaluated the appropriateness of the reasonable and supportable forecast for the current period along with the inputs used in the estimation of expected credit losses.&#160; For the contractual term that extends beyond the reasonable and supportable forecast period, the Company reverts to historical loss information over <em style="font: inherit;">eight</em> quarters using a straight-line approach.&#160; Management <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>apply different reversion techniques depending on the economic environment for the financial asset portfolio and as of the current period has utilized a linear reversion technique.&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b></b></p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>FIRST COMMUNITY BANKSHARES, INC.</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</b></p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Included in its systematic methodology to determine its ACL for loans held for investment and certain off-balance sheet credit exposures, The Company&#160;considers the need to qualitatively adjust expected credit losses for information <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> already captured in the loss estimation process.&#160; These qualitative adjustments either increase or decrease the quantitative model estimation.&#160; Each period the Company considers qualitative factors that are relevant within the qualitative framework that includes the following:&#160; <em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) changes in lending policies and procedures, <em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) changes in economic conditions, <em style="font: inherit;">3</em>) changes in portfolio nature and volume, <em style="font: inherit;">4</em>) changes in management, <em style="font: inherit;">5</em>) changes in past due loans, <em style="font: inherit;">6</em>) changes in the quality of the Company&#8217;s credit review system, <em style="font: inherit;">7</em>) changes in the value of underlying collateral, <em style="font: inherit;">8</em>) the effect of concentrations of credit, and <em style="font: inherit;">9</em>) the effect of other external factors.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">When a loan <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> longer shares similar risk characteristics with its segment, the asset is assessed to determine whether it should be included in another pool or should be individually evaluated. The Company currently maintains a net book balance threshold of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141557982" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="fcbc:MinimumPrincipalBalanceOfLoansForQuarterlyRatingReview" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">500,000</ix:nonFraction> for individually-evaluated loans. Generally, individually-evaluated loans are on nonaccrual status. Based on the threshold above, consumer loans will generally remain in pools unless they meet the dollar threshold and foreclosure is probable. The expected credit losses on individually-evaluated loans will be estimated based on discounted cash flow analysis unless the loan meets the criteria for use of the fair value of collateral, either by virtue of an expected foreclosure or through meeting the definition of collateral-dependent. Financial assets that have been individually evaluated can be returned to a pool for purposes of estimating the expected credit loss insofar as their credit profile improves and that the repayment terms were <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> considered to be unique to the asset.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">When loans are acquired, they are identified as either purchased credit deteriorated ("PCD") or non-PCD.&#160; PCD loans represent assets that are acquired with evidence of more than insignificant credit quality deterioration since the origination of the loans as of the acquisition date.&#160; The ACL for PCD assets is recognized within the business combination accounting&#160;with <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> initial impact to net income.&#160; Changes is estimates of expected credit losses on PCD loans after acquisition are recognized as provision expense (or reversal of provision expense) in subsequent periods as they arise.&#160; &#160; <span style="color:#ff0000;">&#160;&#160;</span></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Non-PCD loans acquired are generally estimated at fair value using a discounted cash flow approach with assumptions of discount rate, remaining life, prepayments, probability of default, and loss given default.&#160; The actual cash flows on these loans could differ materially from the fair value estimates.&#160; The amount we record as the fair values for the loans is generally less than the contractual unpaid principal balance due from the borrowers, with the difference being referred to as the "discount" on the acquired loans.&#160; Discounts on acquired non-PCD loans are accreted to interest income over their estimated remaining lives, which <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include prepayment estimates in certain circumstances.&#160; The ACL for non-PCD assets is recognized as provision expense in the same reporting period as the business combination.&#160; Estimated credit losses for acquired loans are determined using methodologies and applying estimates and assumptions similar to originated performing loans.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">As previously noted, effective <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2023, </em>the Company adopted Financial Accounting Standards Board issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">02,</em> Financial Instruments-Credit Losses (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">326</em>), Troubled Debt Restructurings and Vintage Disclosures.&#160; The allowance for credit losses incorporates an estimate of lifetime credit losses and is recorded on each asset upon origination.&#160; The starting point for the estimate of the allowance for credit losses is historical loss information, which includes losses from modifications of receivables to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty.&#160; The Company uses a probability of default/loss given default model to determine the allowance for credit losses.&#160; An assessment of whether a borrower is experiencing financial difficulty is made at the time of the modification</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Because the effect of most modifications made to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty is already included in the allowance for credit losses, a change to the allowance for credit losses is generally <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> recorded upon modification.&#160; Occasionally, the Company modifies loans by providing principal forgiveness that is deemed to be uncollectible; therefore, that portion of the loan is written off, resulting in a reduction of the amortized cost basis and a corresponding adjustment to the allowance for credit losses.&#160; Additionally, the Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>allow a loan to go interest only for a specified period of time.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company has a variety of assets that have a component that qualifies as an off-balance sheet exposure. These primarily include undrawn portions of revolving lines of credit and standby letters of credit. The expected losses associated with these exposures within the unfunded portion of the loans will be recorded as a liability on the balance sheet with an offsetting income statement expense. The Company&#160;has determined that a majority of the Company&#8217;s off-balance-sheet credit exposures are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> unconditionally cancellable. As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>,&#160;the liability recorded for expected credit losses on unfunded commitments in Other Liabilities was $<ix:nonFraction id="c141557990" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_BalanceSheetLocationAxis-OtherLiabilitiesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OffBalanceSheetCreditLossLiability" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">355</ix:nonFraction>&#160;thousand&#160;compared to $<ix:nonFraction id="c141557991" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_BalanceSheetLocationAxis-OtherLiabilitiesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OffBalanceSheetCreditLossLiability" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">341</ix:nonFraction>&#160;thousand&#160;as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>. &#160;The estimates are determined based on the likelihood of funding during the contractual term and an estimate of credit losses subsequent to funding. Estimated credit losses on subsequently funded balances are based on the same assumptions as used to estimate credit losses on existing funded loans. The current adjustment to the ACL for unfunded commitments is&#160;recognized through provision for credit losses&#160;in the Statement of Income. Prior to <em style="font: inherit;">2023,</em> the current adjustment to the ACL for unfunded commitments was recognized through other operating expense in the Statement of Income.&#160; For additional information, see Note <em style="font: inherit;">6,</em> &#8220;Allowance for Credit Losses,&#8221; to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Item <em style="font: inherit;">8</em> of this report.&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt 0pt 0pt 8pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentPolicyTextBlock" id="c141562241" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Premises and Equipment</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Premises, equipment, and&#160;leases are stated at cost less accumulated depreciation and amortization. Depreciation and amortization are computed using the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of the respective assets. Useful lives range from <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis-FurnitureAndFixturesMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" id="c141557995" format="ixt-sec:duryear">5</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis-FurnitureAndFixturesMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" id="c141557996" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric> years for furniture, fixtures, and equipment; <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis-EquipmentComputerHardwareAndSoftwareMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" id="c141557997" format="ixt-sec:duryear">3</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis-EquipmentComputerHardwareAndSoftwareMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" id="c141557998" format="ixt-sec:duryear">5</ix:nonNumeric> years for computer software, hardware, and data handling equipment; and <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis-BuildingAndBuildingImprovementsMember_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" id="c141557999" format="ixt-sec:duryear">7</ix:nonNumeric> to <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis-BuildingAndBuildingImprovementsMember_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" id="c141558000" format="ixt-sec:duryear">40</ix:nonNumeric> years for buildings and building improvements. Land improvements are amortized over a period of <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PropertyPlantAndEquipmentByTypeAxis-LandAndLandImprovementsMember" name="us-gaap:PropertyPlantAndEquipmentUsefulLife" id="c141558001" format="ixt-sec:duryear">20</ix:nonNumeric> years and leasehold improvements are amortized over the lesser of the term of the respective leases plus the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> optional renewal period, when renewal is reasonably assured, or the estimated useful lives of the improvements. The Company leases various properties within its branch network. Leases generally have initial terms of up to <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseTermOfContract" id="c141558003" format="ixt-sec:duryear">10</ix:nonNumeric> years and most contain options to renew with increases in rent. All leases are accounted for as operating leases. Maintenance and repairs are charged to current operations while improvements that extend the economic useful life of the underlying asset are capitalized. Disposition gains and losses are reflected in current operations.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetsPolicyTextBlock" id="c141562242" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Goodwill and Intangible Assets</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Goodwill and intangible assets which consist of core deposit intangible assets, and other identifiable intangible assets that result from business combinations. Goodwill represents the excess of the purchase price over the fair value of net assets acquired that is allocated to the appropriate reporting unit when acquired.&#160;Core deposit intangible assets represent the future earnings potential of acquired deposit relationships that are amortized over their estimated remaining useful lives. Other identifiable intangible assets primarily represent the rights arising from contractual arrangements that are amortized using the straight-line method.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">An interim analysis of Goodwill is performed&#160;quarterly, and goodwill is tested for impairment annually, on <em style="font: inherit;"> October </em><em style="font: inherit;">31st,</em> or more frequently if events or circumstances indicate there <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be impairment. We have <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141558005">one</span> reporting unit, Community Banking.&#160; If we elect to perform a qualitative assessment, we evaluate factors such as macroeconomic conditions, industry and market considerations, overall financial performance, changes in stock price, and progress towards stated objectives in determining if it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that the fair value of our reporting unit is less than its carrying amount. If we conclude that it is more likely than <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> that the fair value of our reporting unit is less than its carrying amount, a quantitative test is performed; otherwise, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> further testing is required. The quantitative test consists of comparing the fair value of our reporting unit to its carrying amount, including goodwill.&#160;If the fair value of our reporting unit is greater than its book value, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> goodwill impairment exists.&#160;If the carrying amount of our reporting unit is greater than its calculated fair value, a goodwill impairment charge is recognized for the difference.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Management has concluded that there was <ix:nonFraction id="c141558010" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:GoodwillImpairmentLoss" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> goodwill impairment for <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;or&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <ix:exclude>
    <div class="PGFTR" style="text-align: center; width: 100%">

   <ix:exclude>&#160;</ix:exclude>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b></b></p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>FIRST COMMUNITY BANKSHARES, INC.</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</b></p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="fcbc:BankOwnedLifeInsurancePolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c141562243" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Bank Owned Life Insurance</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">The Company has purchased life insurance policies on certain key executives and personnel.&#160; The value recorded on the balance sheet is the amount that can be realized under the insurance contract at the balance sheet date, which is the cash surrender value adjusted for other changes or amounts due that are probable at settlement.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:ComprehensiveIncomePolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c141562244" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Other Comprehensive Income (Loss)&#160;</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">Other comprehensive income (loss)&#160;includes unrealized gains and losses on securities available-for-sale and changes in the funded status of the&#160;nonqualified domestic, noncontributory defined benefit plans which are recognized as separate components of equity.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:CommitmentsAndContingenciesPolicyTextBlock" id="c141562245" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Loss Contingencies</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">Loss contingencies, including claims and legal actions arising in the ordinary course of business, are recorded as liabilities when the likelihood of loss is probable and an amount or range of loss can be reasonable estimated.&#160;&#160;For additional information, see Note <em style="font: inherit;">19,</em> &#8220;Litigation, Commitments, and Contingencies,&#8221; to the Consolidated Financial Statements in Item <em style="font: inherit;">8</em> of this report.&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:RepurchaseAgreementsCollateralPolicy" id="c141562246" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Securities Sold Under Agreements to Repurchase</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Securities sold under agreements to repurchase are generally accounted for as collateralized financing transactions and recognized as short-term borrowings in the Company&#8217;s consolidated balance sheets. Securities, generally U.S. government and federal agency securities, pledged as collateral under these arrangements can be sold or repledged only if replaced by the secured party. The fair value of the collateral provided to a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party is continually monitored and additional collateral is provided as appropriate.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:DerivativesPolicyTextBlock" id="c141562247" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Derivative Instruments</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company primarily uses derivative instruments to protect against the risk of adverse price or interest rate movements on the value of certain assets and liabilities and on future cash flows. Derivative instruments represent contracts between parties that usually require little or <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> initial net investment and result in <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> party delivering cash or another asset to the other party based on a notional amount and an underlying asset as specified in the contract such as interest rates, equity security prices, currencies, commodity prices, or credit spreads. These derivative instruments <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>consist of interest rate swaps, floors, caps, collars, futures, forward contracts, and written and purchased options. Derivative contracts often involve future commitments to exchange interest payment streams or currencies based on a notional or contractual amount, such as interest rate swaps or currency forwards, or to purchase or sell other financial instruments at specified terms on a specified date, such as options to buy or sell securities or currencies. Derivative instruments are subject to counterparty credit risk due to the possibility that the Company will incur a loss because a counterparty, which <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be a bank, a broker-dealer or a customer, fails to meet its contractual obligations. This risk is measured as the expected positive replacement value of contracts. Derivative contracts <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be executed only with exchanges or counterparties approved by the Company&#8217;s Asset/Liability Management Committee.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">If certain conditions are met, a derivative <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be designated as a hedge related to fair value, cash flow, or foreign exposure risk. The recognition of changes in the fair value of a derivative instrument varies depending on the intended use of the derivative and the resulting designation. The Company accounts for hedges of customer loans as fair value hedges. The change in fair value of the hedging derivative and the change in fair value of the hedged exposure are recorded in earnings. Any hedge ineffectiveness is also reflected in current earnings. Changes in the fair value of derivatives <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> designated as hedging instruments are recognized as a gain or loss in earnings. The Company formally documents any relationships between hedging instruments and hedged items and the risk management objective and strategy for undertaking each hedged transaction. All derivative instruments are reported at fair value in the consolidated balance sheets.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationOptionAndIncentivePlansPolicy" id="c141562248" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Equity-Based Compensation</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The cost of employee services received in exchange for equity instruments, including stock options and restricted stock awards, is generally measured at fair value on the grant date. The Black-Scholes-Merton valuation model is used to estimate the fair value of stock options at the grant date while the fair value of restricted stock awards is based on the market price of the Company&#8217;s common stock on the grant date. The Black-Scholes-Merton model incorporates the following assumptions: the expected volatility is based on the weekly historical volatility of the Company&#8217;s common stock price over the expected term of the option; the expected term is generally calculated using the shortcut method; the risk-free interest rate is based on the U.S. Department of the Treasury&#8217;s (&#8220;Treasury&#8221;) yield curve on the grant date with a term comparable to the grant; and the dividend yield is based on the Company&#8217;s dividend yield using the most recent dividend rate paid per share and trading price of the Company&#8217;s common stock. Compensation cost is recognized over the required service period, generally defined as the vesting period for stock option awards and as the restriction period for restricted stock awards. For awards with graded vesting, compensation cost is recognized on a straight-line basis over the requisite service period for the entire award.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>&#160;</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerPolicyTextBlock" id="c141562249" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Revenue Recognition</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Wealth management</i>. Wealth management income represents monthly fees due from wealth management customers in consideration for managing and administrating the customers' assets. Wealth management and trust services include custody of assets, investment management, escrow services, fees for trust services and similar fiduciary activities. Revenue is recognized when the performance obligation is completed each month, which is generally the time that payment is received. Income also includes fees received from a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party broker-dealer as part of a revenue-sharing agreement for fees earned from customers that are referred to the <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party. These fees are paid to the Company by the <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party on a quarterly basis and recognized ratably throughout the quarter as the performance obligation is satisfied.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Service charges on deposits and other service charges and fees</i>.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Service charges on deposits and other service charges and fees represent general service fees for account maintenance and activity and transaction-based fees that consist of transaction-based revenue, time-based revenue (service period), item-based revenue, or some other individual attribute-based revenue. Revenue is recognized when the performance obligation is completed, which is generally monthly for account maintenance services or when a transaction has been completed. Payment for such performance obligations is generally received at the time the performance obligations are satisfied. Other service charges and fees include interchange income from debit and credit card transaction fees.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>&#160;</i></p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b></b></p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>FIRST COMMUNITY BANKSHARES, INC.</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</b></p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:AdvertisingCostsPolicyTextBlock" id="c141562250" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Advertising Expenses</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Advertising costs are generally expensed as incurred. The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>establish accruals for incurred advertising expenses in the course of a fiscal year.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:IncomeTaxPolicyTextBlock" id="c141562251" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Income Taxes</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Income tax expense is comprised of the current and deferred tax consequences of events and transactions already recognized. The Company includes interest and penalties related to income tax liabilities in income tax expense. The effective tax rate, income tax expense as a percent of pre-tax income, <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>vary significantly from statutory rates due to tax credits and permanent differences. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the estimated future tax consequences attributable to differences between the tax bases of assets and liabilities and their carrying amounts for financial reporting purposes. Deferred tax assets and liabilities are adjusted through the provision for income taxes as changes in tax laws or rates are enacted.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i></i></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:EarningsPerSharePolicyTextBlock" id="c141562252" escape="true"><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Per Share Results</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Basic earnings per common share is calculated by dividing net income available to common shareholders by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding during the period. Diluted earnings per common share includes the dilutive effect of potential common stock that could be issued by the Company. Under the treasury stock method of accounting, potential common stock <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be issued for stock options, non-vested restricted stock awards, performance based stock awards, and convertible preferred stock. Diluted earnings per common share is calculated by dividing net income by the weighted average number of common shares outstanding for the period plus the number of dilutive potential common shares. The calculation of diluted earnings per common share excludes potential common shares that have an exercise price greater than the average market value of the Company&#8217;s common stock because the effect would be antidilutive.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;&#160;</p>

   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"></p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i></i></b></p><ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:NewAccountingPronouncementsPolicyPolicyTextBlock" id="c141562253" escape="true"><p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Recent </i></b><b><i>Accounting Standard</i></b><b><i>s</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Standards Adopted&#160;</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2023, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09,</em> &#8220;Income Taxes (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">740</em>).&#8221; The amendments in this ASU are related to the rate reconciliation and income taxes paid disclosures and are designed to improve the transparency of income tax disclosures by requiring (<em style="font: inherit;">1</em>) consistent categories and greater disaggregation of information in the rate reconciliation and (<em style="font: inherit;">2</em>) income taxes paid disaggregated by jurisdiction. The ASU was effective for annual periods beginning <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2025, </em>and was&#160;applied on a prospective basis.&#160; The adoption of this pronouncement did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a material impact on the Consolidated Financial Statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"><i>Standards <em style="font: inherit;">Not</em> Yet Adopted</i></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2024, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">03,</em> "Expense Disaggregation Disclosures (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">230</em>): Disaggregation of Income Statement Expenses". The amendment requires disclosure of disaggregated information about specific expense categories underlying certain income statement expense line items. This ASU will become effective for the Company on <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2027.&#160;</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> July 2025, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">05,</em> "Financial Instruments- Credit Losses (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">326</em>): Measurement of Credit Losses for Accounts Receivable and Contract Assets".&#160; This&#160;amendment introduces a practical expedient available to all entities that permits an entity to assume that existing economic conditions at&#160;the balance sheet date will persist for the remaining life of current accounts receivable and current contract assets, rather than developing a full forward-looking forecast.&#160; This ASU will become effective for the Company in <em style="font: inherit;">2026,</em> on a prospective basis.&#160; The adoption of this pronouncement is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expected to have a material impact on the Company's financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2025, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">08,</em> "Financial Instruments- Credit Losses (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">326</em>): Purchased Loans".&#160; The amendment simplifies accounting for acquired loans under the current expected credit losses (CECL) model by expanding use of the gross-up method to a new category of purchased seasonal loans (PSLs).&#160; &#160;PSLs are acquired loans purchased more than <em style="font: inherit;">90</em> days after origination or acquired in a business combination.&#160; For PSLs, an allowance for credit loss is to be recorded at acquisition with an equal increase to amortized cost and remove credit loss expense on acquisition date.&#160; The ASU does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> apply to credit cards, Topic <em style="font: inherit;">606</em> trade receivables, and debt securities.&#160; The Company expects to early adopt the standard in <em style="font: inherit;">2026,</em> and it is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expected to have a material impact on the Company's financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> November 2025, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09,</em> "Derivatives and Hedging (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">815</em>): Targeted Improvements to Hedge Accounting".&#160; The amendment amends ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">815</em> to clarify, improve, and better align hedge accounting guidance with entities' economic risk management strategies and address implementation challenges in practice.&#160; The ASU is effective for annual reporting periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>with early adoption permitted.&#160; &#160;The adoption of this pronouncement is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expected to have a material impact on the Company's financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2025, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">11,</em> "Interim Reporting (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">270</em>): Narrow-Scope Improvements".&#160; The amendment is to enhance the clarity, navigability, and application of interim reporting guidance in ASC Topic <em style="font: inherit;">270</em> without expanding or reducing the fundamental nature of the interim reporting framework.&#160; The amendments clarify when interim guidance applies, the form and content of interim financial statements, and the related disclosure requirements under GAAP.&#160; The ASU is effective for periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2027, </em>with early adoption permitted.&#160; The adoption of this pronouncement is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expected to have a material impact on the Company's financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">In <em style="font: inherit;"> December 2025, </em>the FASB issued ASU <em style="font: inherit;">No.</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">12,</em> "Codification Improvements".&#160; The amendment consists of technical corrections, clarifications, and narrow-scope improvements that address unintended application issues and improve the clarity and usability of GAAP without making substantive changes to current accounting practice.&#160; The amendments are intended to reduce diversity in practice and correct errors or ambiguous provisions in the Codification.&#160; The ASU is effective for periods beginning after <em style="font: inherit;"> December 15, 2026, </em>with early adoption permitted.&#160; The adoption of this pronouncement is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expected to have a material impact on the Company's financial statements.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> expect other recent accounting standards issued by the FASB or other standards-setting bodies to have a material impact on the consolidated financial statements.</p></ix:nonNumeric><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;"></p>
  </ix:nonNumeric>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">2.</em>&#160; Acquisitions and Divestitures</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company consummated the acquisition of NC-based Surry Bankcorp ("Surrey"), a parent company of Surrey Bank &amp; Trust on <em style="font: inherit;"> April 21, 2023.&#160; </em>The results of operations of the acquired business have been included in the Company's consolidated financial statements since the acquisition date.&#160; All purchase accounting adjustments, transaction-related costs, and integration expenses were recognized in prior years.&#160; <ix:nonFraction id="c141558069" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-SurreyMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationAcquisitionRelatedCosts" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">No</ix:nonFraction> acquisition-related costs or purchase accounting adjustments, related to the Surrey acquisition,&#160;were recorded during the year ended <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
