   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">There were <ix:nonFraction id="c141558079" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromSaleOfAvailableForSaleSecuritiesDebt" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> sales of available for sale debt securities in <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>&#160;nor in <em style="font: inherit;">2024.</em><span style="color:#ff0000;">&#160;</span>&#160;Approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558082" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:ProceedsFromSaleOfAvailableForSaleSecuritiesDebt" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">38.98</ix:nonFraction> million in securities available for sale were sold in <em style="font: inherit;">2023.</em>&#160; Gross gains and gross losses were $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558084" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleRealizedGain" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-7">30</ix:nonFraction> thousand and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558085" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleRealizedLoss" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">51</ix:nonFraction> thousand, respectively for <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2023.&#160; </em>The carrying amount of securities pledged for various purposes totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558086" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PledgedStatusAxis-AssetPledgedAsCollateralMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AvailableForSaleDebtSecuritiesAmortizedCostBasis" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">29.85</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million&#160;as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558087" contextRef="i_2024-12-31_PledgedStatusAxis-AssetPledgedAsCollateralMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AvailableForSaleDebtSecuritiesAmortizedCostBasis" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">24.64</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>.&#160; &#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">In determining whether or <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> a security is impaired, we consider the severity of the loss as well as our intent to hold the securities to maturity or the recovery of the cost basis.&#160; Unrealized losses have <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> been recognized into income as the decline in fair value is largely due to changes in interest rates and other market conditions.&#160; Management does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> intend to sell and it is likely that management will <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> be required to sell the securities prior to their anticipated recovery.&#160;&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>U.S. Treasury securities</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">U.S. Treasury securities are backed by the full faith and credit of the United States government.&#160; On&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the total amortized cost of available for sale U. S. Treasury securities was $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558092" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FinancialInstrumentAxis-USTreasurySecuritiesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AvailableForSaleDebtSecuritiesAmortizedCostBasis" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">10.92</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million.&#160; Based on management's analysis and judgement, there were&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c141558093" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FinancialInstrumentAxis-USTreasurySecuritiesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleAllowanceForCreditLoss" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> credit losses attributable to U.S. Treasury securities on <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Municipal securities</i></p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Municipal securities are securities issued by various&#160;municipalities in the United States.&#160;&#160;At&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the total amortized cost of available for sale Municipal&#160;securities was $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558094" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FinancialInstrumentAxis-USStatesAndPoliticalSubdivisionsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AvailableForSaleDebtSecuritiesAmortizedCostBasis" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">9.29</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million.&#160; The majority of the portfolio&#160;was rated AA or higher, with <ix:nonFraction id="c141558095" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_ExternalCreditRatingByGroupingAxis-ExternalCreditRatingNonInvestmentGradeMember_FinancialInstrumentAxis-USStatesAndPoliticalSubdivisionsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AvailableForSaleDebtSecuritiesAmortizedCostBasis" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> securities rated below investment grade at year-end.&#160;&#160;Based on management's analysis and judgement, there were&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c141558096" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FinancialInstrumentAxis-USStatesAndPoliticalSubdivisionsMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleAllowanceForCreditLoss" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> credit losses attributable to Municipal&#160;securities at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Corporate Notes</i></p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Corporate notes are&#160;debt obligations issued by public or private corporations.&#160; As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, the total amortized cost of available for sale Corporate notes were $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558097" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FinancialInstrumentAxis-CorporateDebtSecuritiesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AvailableForSaleDebtSecuritiesAmortizedCostBasis" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">24.89</ix:nonFraction> million.&#160;&#160;The majority of the portfolio&#160;was rated AA or higher, with <ix:nonFraction id="c141558098" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_ExternalCreditRatingByGroupingAxis-ExternalCreditRatingNonInvestmentGradeMember_FinancialInstrumentAxis-CorporateDebtSecuritiesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:AvailableForSaleDebtSecuritiesAmortizedCostBasis" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> securities rated below investment grade at year-end.&#160;&#160;Based on management's analysis and judgement, there were&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c141558099" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_FinancialInstrumentAxis-CorporateDebtSecuritiesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DebtSecuritiesAvailableForSaleAllowanceForCreditLoss" scale="6" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> credit losses attributable to Corporate note&#160;securities at <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>.</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:FinancingReceivablesTextBlock" id="c3125677" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">5.</em> </b><b>Credit Quality</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company uses a risk grading matrix to assign a risk grade to each loan in its portfolio. Loan risk ratings <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be upgraded or downgraded to reflect current information identified during the loan review process. The general characteristics of each risk grade are as follows:</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width:18pt;vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-size: 10pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">Pass -- This grade is assigned to loans with acceptable credit quality and risk. The Company further segments this grade based on borrower characteristics that include capital strength, earnings stability, liquidity, leverage, and industry conditions.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width:18pt;vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-size: 10pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">Special Mention -- This grade is assigned to loans that require an above average degree of supervision and attention. These loans have the characteristics of an asset with acceptable credit quality and risk; however, adverse economic or financial conditions exist that create potential weaknesses deserving of management&#8217;s close attention. If potential weaknesses are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> corrected, the prospect of repayment <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>worsen.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width:18pt;vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-size: 10pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">Substandard -- This grade is assigned to loans that have well defined weaknesses that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>make payment default, or principal exposure, possible. These loans will likely be dependent on collateral liquidation, secondary repayment sources, or events outside the normal course of business to meet repayment terms.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width:18pt;vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-size: 10pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">Doubtful -- This grade is assigned to loans that have the weaknesses inherent in substandard loans; however, the weaknesses are so severe that collection or liquidation in full is unlikely based on current facts, conditions, and values. Due to certain specific pending factors, the amount of loss cannot yet be determined.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="width:100%;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;"><tbody><tr><td style="width:18pt;">&#160;</td><td style="width:18pt;vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: left; font-size: 10pt;">&#9679;</p> </td><td style="vertical-align:top;"> <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">Loss -- This grade is assigned to loans that will be charged off or charged down when payments, including the timing and value of payments, are uncertain. This risk grade does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> imply that the asset has <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> recovery or salvage value, but simply means that it is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> practical or desirable to defer writing off, either all or a portion of, the loan balance even though partial recovery <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be realized in the future.</p> </td></tr>
</tbody></table>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">ASC <em style="font: inherit;">326</em> prescribes that when an entity determines foreclosure is probable, the expected credit loss is required to be measured based on the fair value of the collateral.&#160; As a practical expedient, an entity <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>use the fair&#160;value as of the reporting date when recording the net carrying amount of the asset.&#160; For the collateral dependent asset ("CDA") a credit loss expense is recorded for loan amounts in excess of fair value of the collateral.&#160; The table below summarizes collateral dependent loans, where foreclosure is possible, by type of collateral, and the extent to which they are collateralized during the periods.&#160; &#160;As noted, as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025, </em><ix:nonFraction id="c141558137" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="fcbc:CollateralDependentLoans" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> loan was&#160;collateral dependent.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>make concessions in interest rates, loan terms and/or amortization terms when restructuring loans for borrowers experiencing financial difficulty. Effective, <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2023, </em>the Company adopted ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">02,</em> Financial Instruments-Credit Losses (Topic <em style="font: inherit;">326</em>), Troubled Debt Restructurings and Vintage Disclosures.&#160; The amendments eliminated TDR accounting guidance for issuers that adopted ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2015</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">13,</em> created a single loan modification accounting model, and clarified disclosure requirements for loan modifications and write-offs.&#160; Presented below are the amortized cost basis and percentage of loan class for loan modifications made to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty by loan class, concession type, and financial effect as of the date indicated.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Upon the Company's determination that a modified loan (or portion of a loan) has subsequently been deemed&#160;uncollectible, the loan (or a portion of the loan) is&#160;written off.&#160; Therefore, the amortized cost basis of the loan is reduced by the uncollectible amount and the allowance for credit losses is adjusted by the same amount.&#160; As of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, there were <ix:nonFraction id="c141558144" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="fcbc:FinancingReceivableModifiedNumberOfLoansUncollectible" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> modified loans (or portions of a loan) deemed uncollectible.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Leases</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Operating leases are recorded as a right of use (&#8220;ROU&#8221;) asset and operating lease liability. The ROU asset is recorded in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141558637"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141558638">other assets</span></span>, while the lease liability is recorded in <span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141558639"><span style="-sec-ix-hidden:c141558640">other liabilities</span></span> on the condensed balance sheet beginning <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2019, </em>when the Company adopted ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2016</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">02,</em> on a prospective basis. The ROU asset represents the right to use an underlying asset during the lease term, and the lease liability represents the obligation to make lease payments arising from the lease. The ROU asset and lease liability have been recognized based on the present value of the lease payments using a discount rate that represented our incremental borrowing rate at the lease commencement date or the date of adoption of ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2016</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">02.</em> The lease expense, which is comprised of the amortization of the ROU asset and the implicit interest accreted on the lease liability, is recognized on a straight-line basis over the lease term and is recorded in occupancy expense in the condensed statements of income.</p>
   <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company&#8217;s current operating leases relate to branch and office locations.&#160;The Company's ROU asset was $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558165" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseRightOfUseAsset" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">591</ix:nonFraction>&#160;thousand&#160;as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, compared to $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558166" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseRightOfUseAsset" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">489</ix:nonFraction>&#160;thousand as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>.&#160; The operating lease liability as of&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, was $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558167" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseLiability" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">591</ix:nonFraction>&#160;thousand&#160;compared to $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558168" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseLiability" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-3">515</ix:nonFraction>&#160;thousand as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>.&#160; The Company&#8217;s total operating leases have remaining terms of <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRemainingLeaseTerm" id="c141558169" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">5</ix:nonNumeric>&#160;months&#160;to <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2025-12-31_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRemainingLeaseTerm" id="c141558170" format="ixt-sec:duryear">5</ix:nonNumeric>&#160;years&#160;compared with&#160;<ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2024-12-31_RangeAxis-MinimumMember" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRemainingLeaseTerm" id="c141558171" format="ixt-sec:durmonth">3</ix:nonNumeric>&#160;to&#160;<ix:nonNumeric contextRef="i_2024-12-31_RangeAxis-MaximumMember" name="us-gaap:LesseeOperatingLeaseRemainingLeaseTerm" id="c141558172" format="ixt-sec:duryear">4.5</ix:nonNumeric>&#160;as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>. The&#160;<em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, weighted average discount was&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c141558173" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseWeightedAverageDiscountRatePercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">3.82</ix:nonFraction>%, compared to&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c141558174" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:OperatingLeaseWeightedAverageDiscountRatePercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="4">3.39</ix:nonFraction>%&#160;from <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em>.</p>

The prepayment or early termination of a repurchase agreement <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>result in substantial penalties based on market conditions.    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b></b></p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>FIRST COMMUNITY BANKSHARES, INC.</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</b></p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><b><span style="background-color:#ffffff">Note <em style="font: inherit;">11</em></span></b><b><span style="background-color:#ffffff">. Derivative Instruments and Hedging Activities</span></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Generally, derivative instruments help the Company manage exposure to market risk and meet customer financing needs. Market risk represents the possibility that fluctuations in external factors such as interest rates, market-driven loan rates, prices, or other economic factors will adversely affect economic value or net interest income.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company has used interest rate swap contracts to modify its exposure to interest rate risk caused by changes in benchmark interest rates in relation to certain designated fixed rate loans. These instruments are used to convert these fixed rate loans to an effective floating rate. If the Secured Overnight Financing Rate ("SOFR") plus a spread falls below the loan&#8217;s stated fixed rate for a given period, the Company will owe the floating rate payer the notional amount times the difference between the floating rate and the stated fixed rate. If SOFR is above the stated rate for a given period, the Company will receive payments based on the notional amount times the difference between the floating rate and the stated fixed rate.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Certain of the Company's interest rate swaps qualify as fair value hedging instruments. Therefore, fair value changes in the derivative and hedged item attributable to the hedged risk are recognized in earnings in the same period. The fair value hedges were effective as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The following table presents the notional, or contractual, amounts and fair values of derivative instruments as of the dates indicated:</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">12</em></b><b>. Employee Benefit Plans</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>&#160;</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Defined Benefit Plans</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>&#160;</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company maintains <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> nonqualified domestic, noncontributory defined benefit plans (the &#8220;Benefit Plans&#8221;) for key members of senior management and non-management directors. The Company&#8217;s unfunded Benefit Plans include the Supplemental Executive Retention Plan (&#8220;SERP&#8221;) and the Directors&#8217; Supplemental Retirement Plan (&#8220;Directors&#8217; Plan&#8221;). The SERP provides for a defined benefit, at normal retirement age, targeted at <ix:nonFraction id="c141558219" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-SupplementalEmployeeRetirementPlanDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:DefinedContributionPlanMaximumAnnualContributionsPerEmployeePercent" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="2">35</ix:nonFraction>% of the participant&#8217;s projected final average compensation, subject to a defined maximum annual benefit. Benefits under the SERP generally become payable at age <ix:nonFraction id="c141558220" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-SupplementalEmployeeRetirementPlanDefinedBenefitMember" unitRef="Pure" name="fcbc:DefinedBenefitPlanEmployeeContributionAge" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">62</ix:nonFraction>. The Directors&#8217; Plan provides for a defined benefit, at normal retirement age, up to <ix:nonFraction id="c141558221" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-DirectorsPlanMember" unitRef="Pure" name="fcbc:DefinedContributionPlanMaximumEmployeeContributionAsPercentageOfBaseSalary" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="0">100</ix:nonFraction>% of the participant&#8217;s highest consecutive <em style="font: inherit;">three</em>-year average compensation. Benefits under the Directors&#8217; Plan generally become payable at age <ix:nonFraction id="c141558223" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-DirectorsPlanMember" unitRef="Pure" name="fcbc:DefinedBenefitPlanEmployeeContributionAge" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">70</ix:nonFraction>. The SERP was frozen near the end of <em style="font: inherit;">2021;</em> the Directors' Plan was fundamentally frozen at that time as well.&#160; &#160;The following table presents the changes in the aggregate actuarial benefit obligation for the <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> plans combined during the periods indicated:</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Deferred Compensation Plan</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company maintains deferred compensation agreements with certain current and former officers that provide benefit payments, over various periods, commencing at retirement or death. There were <ix:nonFraction id="c141558227" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredCompensationArrangementWithIndividualRecordedLiability" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> accrued benefits, which are based on the present values of expected payments and estimated life expectancies, as of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em> or <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>. There was <ix:nonFraction id="c141558229" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredCompensationArrangementWithIndividualCompensationExpense" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="-3">no</ix:nonFraction> deferred compensation plan expense in <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>,&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, or&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>&#160;</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">The Company maintains a deferred compensation plan, referred to as the WRAP, and is a voluntary, non-tax qualified deferred compensation plan available to certain employees, including executive officers. Under the plan, participants <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>defer a portion of their base and/or annual incentive compensation. The plan is intended to mirror the Corporation's qualified KSOP&#160;and <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include discretionary match that coincides with a match made to the KSOP to the extent participants cannot otherwise receive the full match in the KSOP. The balance as of </span><em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em><span style="background-color:#ffffff;"> and </span><em style="font: inherit;">2024</em><span style="background-color:#ffffff;">, was $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558234" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredCompensationPlanAssets" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">11.03</ix:nonFraction></span>&#160;million<span style="background-color:#ffffff;">&#160;and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558235" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:DeferredCompensationPlanAssets" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">8.73</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million,&#160;respectively.</span></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Employee Welfare Plan</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company provides various medical, dental, vision, life, accidental death and dismemberment, and long-term disability insurance benefits to all full-time employees who elect coverage under this program. A <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party administrator manages the health plan. Monthly employer and employee contributions are made to a tax-exempt employee benefits trust where the <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party administrator processes and pays claims. As of <em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em>, stop-loss insurance coverage generally limits the Company&#8217;s risk of loss to $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558238" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="fcbc:StoplossInsuranceLiabilityForIndividualClaims" scale="3" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">200</ix:nonFraction>&#160;thousand&#160;for individual claims and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558239" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="fcbc:StoplossInsuranceLiabilityForAggregateClaims" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">5.65</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million&#160;for aggregate claims. Health plan expenses were $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558240" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OtherPostretirementBenefitExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">4.03</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558242" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OtherPostretirementBenefitExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">4.10</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558244" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:OtherPostretirementBenefitExpense" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">4.16</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Employee Stock Ownership and Savings Plan</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company maintains the Employee Stock Ownership and Savings Plan (&#8220;KSOP&#8221;) that consists of a <em style="font: inherit;">401</em>(k) savings feature that covers all employees that meet minimum eligibility requirements. The Company matches employee contributions at levels determined by the Board of Directors annually. These contributions are made in the <em style="font: inherit;">first</em> quarter following each plan year and employees must be employed on the last day of the plan year to be eligible. Matching contributions to qualified deferrals under the <em style="font: inherit;">401</em>(k) savings component of the KSOP totaled $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558249" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-FourZeroOneKSavingsPlanMember" unitRef="USD" name="fcbc:DefinedBenefitPlanEmployerMatchingContributions" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">2.02</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em>, $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558251" contextRef="d_2024-01-01_2024-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-FourZeroOneKSavingsPlanMember" unitRef="USD" name="fcbc:DefinedBenefitPlanEmployerMatchingContributions" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">1.89</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in <em style="font: inherit;">2024</em>, and $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558253" contextRef="d_2023-01-01_2023-12-31_RetirementPlanTypeAxis-FourZeroOneKSavingsPlanMember" unitRef="USD" name="fcbc:DefinedBenefitPlanEmployerMatchingContributions" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">1.76</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million in <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>. The KSOP held&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c141558255" contextRef="i_2025-12-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesHeldInEmployeeTrustShares" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">271,012</ix:nonFraction>&#160;<span style="font-size: 10pt;">shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock as of </span><em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2025</em><span style="font-size: 10pt;">, <ix:nonFraction id="c141558256" contextRef="i_2024-12-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesHeldInEmployeeTrustShares" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">266,533</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares as of </span><em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2024</em><span style="font-size: 10pt;">, and <ix:nonFraction id="c141558257" contextRef="i_2023-12-31" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:CommonStockSharesHeldInEmployeeTrustShares" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">282,072</ix:nonFraction>&#160;shares as of </span><em style="font: inherit;"> December 31, 2023</em><span style="font-size: 10pt;">.</span></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;"><b><i>Equity-Based Compensation Plans</i></b></p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; text-align: justify;">The Company maintains equity-based compensation plans to promote the long-term success of the Company by encouraging officers, employees, directors, and other individuals performing services for Company to focus on critical long-range objectives. The Company&#8217;s most current equity-based compensation plans include the <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Omnibus Equity Compensation Plan (the <em style="font: inherit;">&#8220;2022</em> Plan&#8221;), which authorized <ix:nonFraction id="c141558260" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_PlanNameAxis-The2022EquitybasedCompensationPlansMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensationArrangementByShareBasedPaymentAwardNumberOfSharesAvailableForGrant" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,000,000</ix:nonFraction> shares for potential grants of Non-Qualified Stock Options, Incentive Stock Options, Performance Shares, Performance Stock Units, Restricted Stock, Restricted Stock Units, and Performance Awards. The Company&#8217;s Compensation and Retirement Committee determines the vesting period for each grant; however, awards shall have a minimum vesting/exercise schedule of at least <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> year, except that a shorter vesting/exercise schedule <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>apply to <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> more than <em style="font: inherit;">5%</em> of the shares authorized for issuance under the <em style="font: inherit;">2022</em> Plan.</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company&#8217;s effective tax rate, income tax as a percent of pre-tax income, <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>vary significantly from the statutory rate due to permanent differences and available tax credits. Permanent differences are income and expense items excluded by law in the calculation of taxable income. The Company&#8217;s most significant permanent differences generally include interest income on municipal securities and increases in the cash surrender value of life insurance policies. The following table reconciles the Company&#8217;s income tax expense&#160;to the amount computed by applying the federal statutory tax rate to pre-tax income for the periods indicated.&#160; The Company adopted ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2023</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">09</em> - Improvements to Income Tax Disclosures on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2025.&#160; </em>The amendments were applied prospectively.&#160; Accordingly, the income tax rate reconciliation for the year ended Decembers <em style="font: inherit;">31,</em> <em style="font: inherit;">2025</em> is presented using the new disclosure requirements.&#160; Prior-period amounts continue to be presented in accordance with the previous guidance.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> July 4, 2025, </em>the One Big Beautiful Bill Act was enacted into law by the federal government.&#160; In accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">740,</em> Income taxes, we recognized the total effect of&#160;the tax law changes.&#160; The tax provision of the One Big Beautiful Act did <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a material impact on our income tax balances.&#160; &#160;</p>

  <ix:nonNumeric contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" name="us-gaap:FairValueMeasurementInputsDisclosureTextBlock" id="c3125732" escape="true">
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b></b></p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>FIRST COMMUNITY BANKSHARES, INC.</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</b></p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">16</em></b><b>. Fair Value&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Financial Instruments Measured at Fair Value</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The following discussion describes the valuation methodologies used for instruments measured at fair value, as well as the general classification of such instruments under the valuation hierarchy.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Assets and Liabilities Reported at Fair Value on a Recurring Basis</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>&#160;</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Available-for-Sale Debt Securities</i>. Debt securities available for sale are reported at fair value on a recurring basis. The fair value of Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> securities is based on quoted market prices in active markets, if available. If quoted market prices are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> available, fair values are measured utilizing independent valuation techniques of identical or similar securities for which significant assumptions are primarily derived from or corroborated by observable market data. Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> securities use fair value measurements from independent pricing services obtained by the Company. These fair value measurements consider observable data that <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include dealer quotes, market spreads, cash flows, the Treasury yield curve, live trading levels, trade execution data, market consensus prepayment speeds, credit information, and bond terms and conditions. The Company&#8217;s Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> securities include U.S. Agency and Treasury securities, municipal securities, and mortgage-backed securities. Securities are based on Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> inputs when there is limited activity or less transparency to the valuation inputs. In the absence of observable or corroborated market data, internally developed estimates that incorporate market-based assumptions are used when such information is available.</p>
   <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Fair value models <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be required when trading activity has declined significantly or does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> exist, prices are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> current, or pricing variations are significant. For Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> securities, the Company obtains the cash flow of specific securities from <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> parties that use modeling software to determine cash flows based on market participant data and knowledge of the structures of each individual security. The fair values of Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> securities are determined by applying proper market observable discount rates to the cash flow derived from <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party models. Discount rates are developed by determining credit spreads above a benchmark rate, such as SOFR, and adding premiums for illiquidity, which are based on a comparison of initial issuance spread to SOFR&#160;versus a financial sector curve for recently issued debt to SOFR. Securities with increased uncertainty about the receipt of cash flows are discounted at higher rates due to the addition of a deal specific credit premium based on assumptions about the performance of the underlying collateral. Finally, internal fair value model pricing and external pricing observations are combined by assigning weights to each pricing observation. Pricing is reviewed for reasonableness based on the direction of specific markets and the general economic indicators.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Equity Securities.</i> Equity securities are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis and included in other assets in the consolidated balance sheets. The Company uses Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> inputs to value equity securities that are traded in active markets. Equity securities that are <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> actively traded are classified in Level <em style="font: inherit;">2.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Loans Held for Investment</i>. Loans held for investment are reported at fair value using the exit price notion, which is derived from <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party models. Loans related to fair value hedges are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Deferred Compensation Assets and Liabilities</i>. Securities held for trading purposes are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis and included in other assets in the consolidated balance sheets. These securities include assets related to employee deferred compensation plans, which are generally invested in Level <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> equity securities. The liability associated with these deferred compensation plans is carried at the fair value of the obligation to the employee, which corresponds to the fair value of the invested assets.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Derivative Assets and Liabilities</i>. Derivatives are recorded at fair value on a recurring basis. The Company obtains dealer quotes, Level <em style="font: inherit;">2</em> inputs, based on observable data to value derivatives.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b></b></p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>FIRST COMMUNITY BANKSHARES, INC.</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</b></p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Assets Measured at Fair Value on a Nonrecurring Basis</i></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><i>Impaired Loans.&#160; </i>Prior to the adoption of ASU <em style="font: inherit;">2016</em>-<em style="font: inherit;">13,</em> impaired loans were recorded at fair value on a nonrecurring basis when repayment is expected solely from the sale of the loan's collateral.&#160; Fair value is based on appraised value adjusted for customized discounting criteria, Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> inputs.</p>
   <p style="background-color:#FFFFFF;font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company maintains an active and robust problem credit identification system. The&#160;review includes obtaining <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party collateral valuations to help management identify potential credit impairment and determine the amount of impairment to record. The Company&#8217;s Special Assets staff manages and monitors all impaired loans. Internal collateral valuations are generally performed within <em style="font: inherit;">two</em> to <em style="font: inherit;">four</em> weeks of identifying the initial potential impairment. The internal valuation compares the original appraisal to current local real estate market conditions and considers experience and expected liquidation costs. The Company typically receives a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party valuation within <em style="font: inherit;">thirty</em> to <em style="font: inherit;">forty-five</em> days of completing the internal valuation. When a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em>-party valuation is received, it is reviewed for reasonableness. Once the valuation is reviewed and accepted, discounts are applied to fair market value, based on, but <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> limited to, our historical liquidation experience for like collateral, resulting in an estimated net realizable value. The estimated net realizable value is compared to the outstanding loan balance to determine the appropriate amount of specific impairment reserve.</p>
   <p style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;"><i>OREO</i>. OREO is recorded at fair value on a nonrecurring basis using Level <em style="font: inherit;">3</em> inputs. The Company calculates the fair value of OREO from current or prior appraisals that have been adjusted for valuation declines, estimated selling costs, and other proprietary qualitative adjustments that are deemed necessary.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note <em style="font: inherit;">19</em></b><b>.</b><b> </b><b>Litigation, Commitments</b><b>,</b><b> and Contingencies</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Litigation</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">On <em style="font: inherit;"> May 6, 2024, </em>the Bank agreed to settle a putative class action lawsuit pending in the United States District Court for the Southern District of West Virginia, filed on <em style="font: inherit;"> June 24, 2022. </em>The civil action alleges the Bank breached its deposit account agreements and was unjustly enriched by collecting overdraft fees with respect to certain debit card transactions and by assessing more than <em style="font: inherit;">one</em> nonsufficient funds fee on items presented multiple times for payment. The Bank denies each and every substantive allegation asserted in the civil action. Under the settlement, which is subject to documentation and preliminary and final court approval, the Bank agrees to establish a $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558382" contextRef="i_2024-05-06_LitigationCaseAxis-ClassActionLawsuitMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:LossContingencyAccrualAtCarryingValue" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-5">4.80</ix:nonFraction> million settlement fund and forgive up to $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558383" contextRef="d_2024-05-06_2024-05-06_LitigationCaseAxis-ClassActionLawsuitMember" unitRef="USD" name="fcbc:LitigationSettlementFeeExpenseForgiven" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">500,000</ix:nonFraction> in assessed but unpaid fees. Attorneys&#8217; fees, settlement administration expenses, and settlement payments to eligible class members will be paid from the settlement fund. Under the settlement, the Bank admitted <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> wrongdoing and will receive a complete release of all claims asserted in the civil action. The Bank agreed to the settlement in order to resolve the litigation and avoid further expense.&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company and its subsidiaries are currently involved in various legal proceedings in the normal course of business. On at least a quarterly basis, the Company&#160;assesses its liabilities and contingencies in connection with all pending or threatened claims and litigation, utilizing the most recent information available. On a matter-by-matter basis, an accrual for loss is established for those matters which the Company&#160;believes it is probable that a loss <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be incurred and that the amount of such loss can be reasonably estimated. Once established, each accrual is adjusted as appropriate to reflect any subsequent developments. Accordingly, management&#8217;s estimate will change from time to time, and actual losses <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>be more or less than the current estimate. For matters where a loss is <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> probable, or the amount of the loss cannot be estimated, <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> accrual is established.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">We are&#160;currently a defendant in other legal actions and asserted claims in the normal course of business. Although we are unable to assess the ultimate outcome of each matter with certainty, we believe that the resolution of these actions should <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> have a material adverse effect on our financial position, results of operations, or cash flows.</p>

   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b></b></p><ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>FIRST COMMUNITY BANKSHARES, INC.</b></p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</b></p></ix:exclude><p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: center;"><b></b></p>
   <p style="font-family: 'Times New Roman', Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: left"><b><i>&#160;</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b><i>Commitments and Contingencies</i></b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company is a party to financial instruments with off balance sheet risk in the normal course of business to meet the financing needs of its customers. These financial instruments include commitments to extend credit, standby letters of credit, and financial guarantees. These instruments involve, to varying degrees, elements of credit and interest rate risk beyond the amount recognized in the consolidated balance sheets. The contractual amounts of these instruments reflect the extent of involvement the Company has in particular classes of financial instruments. If the other party to a financial instrument does <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> perform, the Company&#8217;s credit loss exposure is the same as the contractual amount of the instrument. The Company uses the same credit policies in making commitments and conditional obligations as it does for on balance sheet instruments.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Commitments to extend credit are agreements to lend to a customer as long as there is <em style="font: inherit;">no</em> violation of any condition established in the contract. Commitments generally have fixed expiration dates or other termination clauses and <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>require payment of a fee. Since many commitments are expected to expire without being drawn on, the total commitment amounts do <em style="font: inherit;">not</em> necessarily represent future cash requirements. The amount of collateral obtained, if deemed necessary, is based on management&#8217;s credit evaluation of each customer on a case-by-case basis. Collateral <em style="font: inherit;"> may </em>include accounts receivable, inventory, property, plant and equipment, and income producing commercial properties. The Company maintains a reserve for the risk inherent in unfunded lending commitments, which is included in other liabilities in the consolidated balance sheets.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">Standby letters of credit and financial guarantees are conditional commitments issued by the Company to guarantee the performance of a customer to a <em style="font: inherit;">third</em> party. The credit risk involved in issuing letters of credit is essentially the same as that involved in extending credit to customers. The amount of collateral obtained, if deemed necessary, to secure the customer&#8217;s performance under certain letters of credit is based on management&#8217;s credit evaluation of the customer.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The following table presents the off-balance sheet financial instruments as of the dates indicated:</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>Note </b><b><em style="font: inherit;">20</em></b><b>.</b><b> </b><b>Regulatory Requirements </b><b>and Restrictions&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;"><b>&#160;</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The Company and the Bank are subject to various regulatory capital requirements administered by state and federal banking agencies. Failure to meet minimum capital requirements can initiate certain mandatory and possibly additional discretionary actions by regulators that, if undertaken, could have a direct material effect on the Company&#8217;s consolidated financial statements. Under the capital adequacy guidelines and the regulatory framework for prompt corrective action, which applies only to the Bank, the Bank must meet specific capital guidelines that involve quantitative measures of the entity&#8217;s balance sheet assets and off-balance sheet items as calculated under regulatory accounting practices. The Bank&#8217;s capital amounts and classifications are also subject to qualitative judgments by the regulators about components, risk weightings, and other factors. In addition, the Company and the Bank are subject to various regulatory restrictions related to the payment of dividends, including requirements to maintain capital at or above regulatory minimums.</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">The current risk-based capital requirements, based on the international capital standards known as Basel III, requires the Company and the Bank to maintain minimum amounts and ratios of Common Equity Tier <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> capital, Tier <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> capital, and total capital to risk-weighted assets, and of Tier <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> capital to average consolidated assets (&#8220;Tier <em style="font: inherit;">1</em> leverage ratio&#8221;), as defined in the regulations.&#160; Basel III&#8217;s capital conservation buffer (&#8220;CCB&#8221;), which is intended to absorb losses during periods of economic stress, increased those minimum ratios by&#160;<ix:nonFraction id="c141558399" contextRef="i_2019-01-01" unitRef="Pure" name="fcbc:CapitalConservationBuffer" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="3">2.5</ix:nonFraction>% on <em style="font: inherit;"> January 1, 2019.</em></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:justify;">&#160;</p>

   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;"><b>Note </b><b><em style="font: inherit;">21</em></b><b>.</b><b>&#160;Segment Information</b></p>
   <p style="font-family:'Times New Roman', Times, serif;font-size:10pt;margin:0pt;text-align:left;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company conducts its business activities through community banking. Community banking revolves around serving the community and customers where the bank has branches and offices. Community banking consists of commercial and consumer banking, lending activities, and wealth management.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The Company&#8217;s&#160;chief executive officer&#160;is in charge of allocating the Company&#8217;s resources and assessing the Company's performance, and as such, has been identified as the chief operating decision maker. The chief operating decision maker regularly reviews a multitude of reports that have a varying level of combined detail on products offered, however, all of the information and activity reviewed fall under the definition of community banking.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Based on the business activities and information reviewed by the chief operating decision maker, the Company has&#160;<em style="font: inherit;">one</em>&#160;reportable segment - Community Banking.</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The accounting policies of the community banking segment are the same as those for the Company described in Note <em style="font: inherit;">1.</em>&#160;In accordance with ASC <em style="font: inherit;">280,</em> the Company has concluded that&#160;consolidated net income&#160;is the measure of segment profit or loss that is required to be reported because it is the measure determined in accordance with measurement principles that are most consistent with US GAAP. As the Company only has <ix:nonFraction id="c141558407" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31" unitRef="Pure" name="us-gaap:NumberOfReportableSegments" scale="0" format="ixt-sec:numwordsen" decimals="INF">one</ix:nonFraction> reportable segment, total segment net income and total segment assets are equivalent to the results disclosed in the accompanying Consolidated Statements of Income and Consolidated Balance Sheets, respectively</p>
   <p style="text-align: justify; font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
   <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>

    <b>Note </b>
    <b><em style="font: inherit;">24</em></b>
    <b>.</b>
    <b>&#160;Subsequent Events</b>
   </div>
   <div style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">
     &#160;
   </div>
   <div style="margin: 0pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt;">
    <div style="font-size: 10pt;">
      On
     <em style="font: inherit;"> January 23, 2026, </em>the Company completed its previously announced merger (the &#8220;Merger&#8221;) with Hometown Bancshares, Inc. a West Virginia corporation headquartered in Middlebourne, West Virginia (&#8220;Hometown&#8221;), pursuant to an Agreement and Plan of Merger (the &#8220;Agreement&#8221;) dated
     <em style="font: inherit;"> July 19, 2025, </em>by and between the company&#160;and Hometown.&#160; At the Effective Time, Hometown merged with and into the Company, with the Company&#160;as the surviving corporation in the Merger.
    </div>
    <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt;">&#160;</p>
    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Immediately following the Merger, Union Bank, Inc., a wholly-owned subsidiary of Hometown, merged with and into First Community Bank, a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company&#160;(the &#8220;Bank Merger&#8221;), with First Community Bank as the surviving bank in the Bank Merger.</p>
    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; font-size: 10pt; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">Pursuant to the Agreement,&#160;each outstanding share of common stock of Hometown was converted into the right to receive <ix:nonFraction id="c141558415" contextRef="i_2026-01-23_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesMember_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" unitRef="Pure" name="fcbc:BusinessCombinationStockConversionRatio" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">11.706</ix:nonFraction> shares (the &#8220;Exchange Ratio&#8221;) of the Company's&#160;common stock, par value $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558416" contextRef="i_2026-01-23_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesMember_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" unitRef="USDPerShare" name="us-gaap:CommonStockParOrStatedValuePerShare" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1.00</ix:nonFraction> per share, plus cash, without interest, in lieu of fractional shares.&#160; In connection with the transaction, the Company issued <ix:nonFraction id="c141558417" contextRef="d_2026-01-23_2026-01-23_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesMember_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" unitRef="Share" name="us-gaap:BusinessAcquisitionEquityInterestsIssuedOrIssuableNumberOfSharesIssued" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,029,314</ix:nonFraction> common shares and paid $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558418" contextRef="d_2026-01-23_2026-01-23_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesMember_SubsequentEventTypeAxis-SubsequentEventMember" unitRef="USD" name="fcbc:BusinessCombinationCashPaidForFractionalShares" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="INF">1,384.96</ix:nonFraction> in cash in lieu of issuing <em style="font: inherit;">41.404</em> fractional shares.</p>
    <p style="font-size: 10pt; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;, Times, serif; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">&#160;</p>
    <p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt; text-align: justify;">At the end of <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em>&#160;Hometown had total assets of approximately $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558421" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:Assets" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">415</ix:nonFraction> million, loans of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558422" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:NotesReceivableNet" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">172</ix:nonFraction> million and deposits of $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558423" contextRef="i_2025-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:Deposits" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-6">376</ix:nonFraction> million.&#160; The transaction will be&#160;accounted for using&#160;the acquisition method of accounting and, accordingly, assets acquired, liabilities assumed, and consideration exchanged will be&#160;recorded at their preliminary estimated fair value on the acquisition date. Fair values are preliminary and subject to refinement for up to a year after the closing date of the acquisition. The Company incurred $<ix:nonFraction id="c141558424" contextRef="d_2025-01-01_2025-12-31_BusinessAcquisitionAxis-HometownBancsharesMember" unitRef="USD" name="us-gaap:BusinessCombinationAcquisitionRelatedCosts" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" decimals="-4">2.91</ix:nonFraction> million&#160;of merger expense in <em style="font: inherit;">2025,</em>&#160;with the costs being&#160;primarily related to data conversion, investment banking fees, and legal fees.&#160;&#160;</p>

<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">Stockholders and the Board of Directors of First Community Bankshares, Inc.</p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;">Bluefield, Virginia</p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; margin: 0pt;"><b>Opinions on the Financial Statements and Internal Control over Financial Reporting</b></p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of First Community Bankshares, Inc. (the "Company") as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, the related consolidated statements of income, comprehensive income, changes in stockholders&#8217; equity, and cash flows for each of the years in the three-year period ended December 31, 2025, and the related notes (collectively referred to as the "financial statements"). We also have audited the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025, based on criteria established in Internal Control &#8211; Integrated Framework: (2013) issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO).</p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">In our opinion, the financial statements referred to above present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company as of December 31, 2025 and 2024, and the results of its operations and its cash flows for each of the years in the three-year period ended December 31, 2025 in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America. Also in our opinion, the Company maintained, in all material respects, effective internal control over financial reporting as of December 31, 2025, based on criteria established in Internal Control &#8211; Integrated Framework: (2013) issued by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO).</p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;"><b>Basis for Opinions</b></p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">The Company&#8217;s management is responsible for these financial statements, for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting, and for its assessment of the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting, included in the accompanying Management&#8217;s Assessment of Internal Control over Financial Reporting. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company&#8217;s financial statements and an opinion on the Company&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting based on our audits. We are a public accounting firm registered with the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) ("PCAOB") and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB.</p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audits to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud, and whether effective internal control over financial reporting was maintained in all material respects.</p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
<p style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 10pt; font-variant: normal; text-align: justify; margin: 0pt;">Our audits of the financial statements included performing procedures to assess the risks of material misstatement of the financial statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing procedures that respond to those risks. Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. Our audits also included evaluating the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of the financial statements. Our audit of internal control over financial reporting included obtaining an understanding of internal control over financial reporting, assessing the risk that a material weakness exists, and testing and evaluating the design and operating effectiveness of internal control based on the assessed risk. Our audits also included performing such other procedures as we considered necessary in the circumstances. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinions.</p>
<p style="font-family:'Times New Roman';font-size:10pt;font-variant:normal;margin:0pt;">&#160;</p>
